DFT calculations show that the process involves an unstable intermediate, U V O 2 + -AcOH template, which is prompt to disproportionation into inactive U IV and appears to be responsible for the low TON, which is reported. However, the speciation studies also suggest that the equatorial environment of UO 2 2+ would stabilize this UV intermediate and therefore influence the CH 4 production as well as decreasing the potential additional competitive paths, leading to greater selectivity.
items.authors: Eachann Assendjee, Thayalan Rajeshkumar, Lhoussain Khrouz, Yoann Fréroux, Cyrille Monnereau, Olivier Maury

items.title: Towards an Accurate Atomistic Description of Procaine Crystals: Force Field Development and MD Simulation of Solid-to-Liquid Phase Transitions
items.abstract: Rational design of crystalline materials is crucial for material science and pharmaceutical development, requiring molecular modeling as a powerful complementary tool. This study employs molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the thermal stability, structural evolution, and melting mechanisms of crystalline procaine base across a temperature range of 23 to 373 K. To evaluate potential finite-size and boundary effects, two distinct computational setups were considered: a bulk crystal model under periodic boundary conditions (System I, 600 molecules) and an isolated nanocrystal in vacuum (System II, 1188 molecules). Both systems demonstrate well-preserved long-range positional ordering from 23 to 313 K, followed by the appearance of a plastic crystalline state with enhanced rotational freedom between 323 and 333 K. At 343 K, a heterogeneous, surface-initiated phase transition to an isotropic melt occurs, which closely matches the experimental melting point of procaine free-base of 334-337 K. MD analysis reveals remarkably slow melting kinetics at 333-343 K, where a crystalline core persists for over 300 ns before complete melting at 500 ns. We found that the thermal breakdown of the crystal lattice strongly correlates with a breakage of the intermolecular hydrogen-bonding 3D network between procaine molecules. Radial distribution function (RDF) analysis shows a sharp shift in the primary amino nitrogen correlations (N10···N10) towards short-distances upon melting, whereas short-range hydrogen-bond N10···O9 distances remain spatially invariant in the liquid phase. Mean square displacement (MSD) of procaine molecules demonstrates a dramatic transition from restricted lattice vibrations below 333 K to active fluid diffusion above 343 K. These findings are accompanied by rotational autocorrelation functions transition from long-time orientational persistence in the solid state (23-333 K) to rapid exponential relaxation in the melt (343-373 K). Finally, unconstrained melting of System II produces a spherical nanodroplet driven by surface tension minimization, confirming that the performance of the developed OPLS-AA FF model.
items.authors: Viktoriia O. Chukhlib, Viktor V. Tokariev, Alexander Kyrychenko

items.title: Polymorphous Structural Landscapes Drive Broadband Optical Response in Water-Stable Mixed-Halide Antiperovskites
items.abstract: Silver chalcohalide antiperovskites have emerged as low-toxicity semiconductors with strong near-infrared absorption, although their unusual composition-dependent optical properties, including inverse bandgap bowing, remain poorly understood. Here, Ag3SI1-xBrx solid solutions were synthesized by a solvent-free mechanochemical route and investigated by structural and optical characterization, ultrafast spectroscopy, and first-principles calculations. While all compositions retain an average cubic Pm-3m structure and exhibit a Vegard-like lattice contraction with increasing Br content, strongly nonlinear optical behavior and multiple absorption onsets are observed. First principles calculations reveal that these alloys are more appropriately described by an ensemble of electronically distinct low-energy configurations arising from an underlying polymorphous energy landscape. This configurational diversity redistributes band-edge spectral weight, enables quasi-direct transitions at Γ, and provides a microscopic explanation for the broadband absorption and anomalous bandgap evolution. Transient absorption spectroscopy further supports the presence of different compositiondependent electronic environments and reveals prolonged carrier lifetimes for mixed-halides, consistent with alloy-disorder-induced localization. From an applicative perspective, these materials show remarkable water stability and efficient photothermal energy conversion enabling their use in a proof-of-concept solar water evaporation setup. These findings establish Ag3SI1-xBrx antiperovskites as water-stable, low-toxicity, broadband-absorbing materials and demonstrate the importance of polymorphous local structure in governing their optical response.
items.authors: Sahiba Bano, Ghita Khatiri, Mitisha Jain, Prince Sharma, Saurabh Saini, Byeongchan Lee

items.title: Single-Ion Hydration Through the Lens of Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials
items.abstract: Single-ion hydration provides a stringent test of molecular models because local ionwater interactions, collective polarization, nuclear quantum effects, and long-range electrostatics all contribute to experimentally measurable structure, spectra, and thermodynamics. Here we discuss how data-driven many-body potentials, in particular MB-pol for water and MB-nrg for hydrated ions, provide a physically transparent route from correlated electronic structure data to predictive simulations of ion hydration from clusters to bulk water and aqueous interfaces. We emphasize how this framework transforms single-ion hydration from a parameterization problem into a hierarchy of many-body observables, and we outline opportunities for connecting simulations directly with interfacial spectroscopy, hydration free energies, and complex electrolyte environments.
items.authors: Francesco Paesani, Suman Saha, Richa Rashmi, Henry Agnew, Xuanyu Zhu, Olivia Zhou

items.title: Red TADF Pyridoquinoxaline-Annulated Curved Nitrogen-Doped PAHs and their use in OLEDs
items.abstract: Curved nitrogen-doped polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons offer a rigid and nonplanar framework for investigating how donor identity regulates the balance between locally excited and charge-transfer states in thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters. Here, a pyrido[2,3b]quinoxaline unit was integrated into a dibenzo[b,f]azepine-based polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold and functionalized with one of 3,6-di- tert -butylcarbazole ( TBCzPyN-PAH ), diphenylamine ( DPAPyN-PAH ), 9,9-dimethyl-9,10-dihydroacridine ( DMAcPyN-PAH ), or phenoxazine ( PXZPyN-PAH ) donor moieties. The resulting series provides a common acceptor framework in which the electronic and conformational properties of the peripheral donor affect the 2 energies of the excited states. Donor substitution tunes the emission maximum in toluene from 528 to 697 nm. In 2 wt% doped films in CBP, these compounds emit from 519 to 622 nm with PLQY of up to 58%. Temperature-dependent time-resolved photoluminescence confirms TADF for all investigated compounds except for the DPA derivative. Across the TADF-active series, the singlet–triplet energy gap, Δ E ST , decreases from 0.22 to 0.03 eV and the delayed fluorescence lifetime shortens from 8.5 ms to 29 μs. Vacuum-deposited OLEDs with TBCzPyN-PAH showed EQE max , of 21.6% at an electroluminescence maximum of 538 nm, whereas the device with PXZPyN-PAH emitted at 606 nm and showed a lower EQE max of 7.2% but with a milder efficiency roll-off.
items.authors: Jakub Wagner, Eglė Tankelevičiūtė, Haoyang Li, Tomas Matulaitis, Maja Morawiak, Maciej Jelecki

items.title: A spectral reset law explains and predicts periodic recurrence in the elements
items.abstract: The recurrence of chemical properties is the defining feature of the periodic system, yet it is conventionally explained only indirectly, through inferred electron configurations and heuristic filling rules rather than being directly derived from atomic observables. Building on an empirical spectral framework in which elements occupy a bounded spectral space defined by two measured frequencies, the K-edge frequency (𝜈 max ) and the first ionization frequency (𝜈 ion ), we show that recurrence arises from simple quantitative constraints operating directly on these observables. As 𝜈 max increases across the elemental sequence, 𝜈 ion rises toward the upper boundary of the spectral space. At this limiting condition, a spectral mode bifurcates and 𝜈 ion undergoes a sharp reset toward a nearly invariant baseline, cancelling the accumulated rise to within 1%. Repetition of this rise–split–reset structure partitions spectral space into successive bounded intervals that emerge as periods, with lower and upper edges corresponding to elements conventionally classified as Groups 1 and 18, respectively. The rise–split–reset structure yields the recurrence 𝜈 ion (𝑛 + 1) = 𝜈 ion (𝑛) + Δ𝜈 ion (rise) − Δ𝜈 ion (reset) , with |Δ𝜈 ion | = 𝐴𝜈 𝑚𝑎𝑥 𝑏 , so that successive period anchors recur at the same relative position in spectral space. Across the four experimental period boundaries, reset magnitude scales linearly with the spectral splitting amplitude (𝑅 2 = 0.962), empirically linking the recurrence to the mode differentiation that establishes the periods. Seeded with a single measured value (lithium), the recursion regenerates the experimental G1 and G18 period anchors with a median error of 1.4%, and extrapolates beyond the known table to hypothetical periods 8 and 9, including element 119 at 𝜈 ion = (1.12 ± 0.33) × 10 15 s −1 (4.6 ± 1.4 eV). These results establish periodic recurrence as a quantitative, generative spectral structure in measurement space and show that ionization frequencies are not independent quantities, but are determined sequentially from a single seed and a pair of spectral scaling power laws with only two measured observables.
items.authors: Abdennour Abbas

items.title: Nano-Focusing of Fiber-Guided Vortex Beam using Plasmonic Nanoantennas
items.abstract: Optical vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) and cylindrical vector beams (CVBs) enable unique functionalities in optical communication, sensing, and chiral light-matter interactions. However, their use at the nanoscale is hindered by a spatial mismatch between the micron-scale beam and nanoscale targets, limiting light-matter coupling. In this study, we investigate a fiber-integrated plasmonic platform that confines fiber-guided vortex modes to subwavelength dimensions using a radially symmetric gold nanorod array on a polarization-maintaining ring-core vortex fiber facet. Full-vectorial finite-element simulations examine the coupling of radially polarized (TM 01 ), azimuthally polarized (TE 01 ), and circularly polarized (CP) OAM modes to the nanostructure array. The simulations predict symmetry-selective field enhancement and confinement to a ~300 nm central region (spatial confinement factor ~13), while preserving the polarization state, and helical phase of the OAM beam. The TM 01 mode yields the strongest enhancement through symmetry matching with the radial array, the CP-OAM modes show comparable enhancement and helicity-independent confinement, and the TE 01 mode couples weakly. Experimentally, we fabricate the nanostructure array on the fiber facet and characterize the transmitted modes in the far-field, where polarization-projection and coaxial interference measurements verify stable far-field propagation with nominal circular-polarization and topological charge magnitude | l |. These results establish a compact, scalable platform for predicted subwavelength confinement of structured light toward nanoscale light-matter interaction and chiral sensing.
items.authors: Rohil Kayastha, Wei Zhang, Blake Birmingham, Aaron P. Greenberg, Zhi Gao, Rafael Quintero-Torres

items.title: SimSJSAlert: A Similarity-Augmented Multi-View Learning Framework with Scaffold Alerts for Drug-Induced Stevens-Johnson Syndrome Risk Assessment
items.abstract: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a rare, life-threatening adverse drug reaction for which early identification of high-risk drugs remains challenging. In this study, we developed an explainable quantitative structure-toxicity relationship (QSTR) framework for SJS prediction using a multi-view learning framework with 21 molecular representations, including molecular descriptors, fingerprints, transformer-based embeddings, and a molecular similarity representation. Model development and evaluation were designed in accordance with the OECD principles for QSAR validation, incorporating scaffold-aware validation, external evaluation on pharmacovigilance negative-signal compounds, and structural interpretation by integrating SHAP with Bemis-Murcko scaffold enrichment analysis. The proposed framework achieved robust sensitivity and specificity, with molecular similarity consistently improving the identification of SJS-associated compounds. Furthermore, a consensus prediction and scaffold-based prioritization strategy identified several high-risk drugs from the 1 external negative-signal dataset, including cefprozil, tetracycline, and omadacycline, highlighting their potential association with SJS and warranting further pharmacovigilance and experimental investigation. To facilitate practical application, this was deployed as a freely accessible web server, SimSJSAlert (https: //sim-sjs-alert.streamlit.app/), enabling rapid drug-induced SJS risk assessment. The proposed framework combines predictive performance, interpretability, and accessibility to support early SJS risk assessment, pharmacovigilance signal prioritization, and safer drug development.
items.authors: Huynh Anh Duy, Sastiya Kampaengsri, Supreeya Paiboon, Tarapong Srisongkram

items.title: Full-scale Hazardous Waste Incineration of PFAS in Fluorotelomer-Based Aqueous Film-Forming Foam
items.abstract: In the absence of full-scale incineration studies into the impacts of temperature on thermal destruction of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), globally evolving regulatory guidelines have been inconsistent. In this study, we incinerated a fluorotelomerization-based aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF) concentrate at different temperatures and feed rates of up to 1500 kg/h in one of the largest hazardous waste incinerators in the world. At secondary combustion chamber temperatures as low as 950 °C and 2 seconds gas residence time, the destruction and removal efficiency for the main AFFF component 6:2 fluorotelomer sulfonamide alkylbetaine (6:2 FTAB, a.k.a. Capstone B) exceeded 99.999999% at the highest AFFF feed rate. Non-polar volatile fluorinated compounds targeted by Other Test Method 50 (OTM-50) were below method detection limits, while PFAS concentrations in ashes and scrubber waters were practically indistinguishable from baseline conditions when no fluorine-containing waste was incinerated. PFAS stack emissions into the atmosphere during AFFF treatment were substantially lower than volatile PFAS emissions from a typical landfill. Quantum chemical modeling suggested that a similar treatment efficiency may be expected for perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS)-based electrochemical fluorination foams. The findings of our study suggest that hazardous waste incineration may be effective at temperatures well below the 1100 °C required by some current regulations, minimizing fuel consumption, equipment wear, and undesirable side reactions during thermal PFAS destruction.
items.authors: Jens Blotevogel, Wenchao Lu, Anthony K. Rappé, Olaf Holm, Marco Gross, Peter Leube

items.title: BondNet: Noise-Robust Molecular Bond Perception from 3D Coordinates with Explicit Hydrogen Context
items.abstract: Recovering molecular graphs from atomic identities and 3D coordinates is a key step in coordinate-first molecular modelling and generation. We present Bond-Net, a two-stage framework in which a PaiNN model first predicts connectivity on a distance-derived candidate graph and a topology-aware network then classifies heavy–heavy bond types. Explicit hydrogens participate in message passing as local valence context but are excluded from bond-type supervision and scoring. On a fixed 26,940-molecule GEOM-DRUGS validation cohort, the near-clean model achieves pipeline macro-F1 = 0.9994 and correctly types every reference heavy–heavy bond in 99.4% of molecules. A historical ablation shows that removing hydrogen context reduces macro-F1 by 6.7 percentage points and the exact-type rate to 19.7%. With Gaussian coordinate-noise augmentation and candidate graphs rebuilt from the perturbed coordinates, BondNet retains pipeline macro-F1 = 0.9859 and a true-bond exact-type rate of 87.7% at σ = 0.1 Å; its stricter HH-graph exact match is 83.0% because extra predicted bonds are also penalized. BondNet’s pipeline macro-F1 exceeds RDKit DetermineBonds at every tested noise level on the common denominator. Residual strict-label disagreements are concentrated in resonance-ambiguous N–O and carboxyl motifs. An exact-molecule-leakage-controlled diversity study further shows that a curated multi-source set of 80,000 molecules transfers better than both a same-size random GEOM subset and a 3.4× larger single-source set. 1 Scientific Contribution. BondNet isolates geometric connectivity from topology-aware bond typing and quantifies how explicit-hydrogen context and noise augmentation affect robust graph recovery. The study also provides atom-pair-matched baselines, explicitly reports tool failures, and introduces an exact-molecule-leakage-controlled comparison of training-set diversity and scale.
items.authors: Xiaochen Zhang, Hui Zeng, Xiao-Chen Zhang

items.title: All-Dielectric Metasurfaces in Fundamentals, Materials, and Emerging Applications
items.abstract: The field of optics is undergoing a transformative shift, pushed forward by the demand for miniaturized, lightweight, and highly functional components. Dielectric metasurfaces have emerged as a transformative platform in modern photonics, offering unprecedented control over the amplitude, phase, polarization, and frequency of light within an ultrathin, planar architecture. Unlike their metallic predecessors, all-dielectric metasurfaces exploit Mie resonances, bound states in the continuum, and multipolar interference to achieve low-loss, high-efficiency optical functionalities across the visible, near-infrared, and terahertz spectral ranges. This review covers the field systematically, starting with the common working principles of dielectric metasurfaces and the physical mechanisms that make them so versatile. We then discuss the most widely used material platforms, including their optical properties and practical trade-offs, followed by an overview of the fabrication techniques available today. We look at both traditional top-down methods, such as electron-beam lithography, and emerging high-throughput approaches like nanoimprint lithography and photochemical deposition. We also examine the design strategies and element geometries used to build optical functionality into these surfaces, from simple phase-shifting pillars to more complex resonant architectures. Finally, this review examines the broad range of applications these structures enable, from metalenses and holography to nonlinear optics, biosensing, and terahertz generation. By identifying the key open challenges in fabrication scalability, broadband operation, and active tunability, this review aims to serve both as a reference resource for specialists and as an entry point for researchers from adjacent disciplines, charting a clear roadmap for the next decade of flat-optics research.
items.authors: Rana Faryad Ali

items.title: Three-photon Absorption Cross-Sections of Serotonin, Fluorescein, Rhodamine 6G, and Some Fluorescent Protein Chromophores
items.abstract: Interest in studying, enhancing the performance, and engineering of three-photon absorption (3PA) responsive molecular probes and bio-molecular systems, such as fluorescent proteins (FPs), has increased significantly over the last decade. 3PA has a deeper penetration than one-and two-photon absorption (1PA and 2PA, respectively). In particular, FPs can display 3PA within the deep tissue imaging window (1600-1870 nm). Experimentally, the 3PA ability (measured in terms of the 3PA cross-section, σ 3PA ) of a set of red fluorescent proteins (RFPs) has been reported before. On the other hand, just a handful of computational studies have determined the 3PA response and, in even fewer cases, determined the σ 3PA of selected FPs. By means of time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) here we determine the σ 3PA of fluorescein, rhodamine 6G, serotonin, and a curated set of isolated FP chromophores for which their computationally determined 1PA and 2PA have been reported previously. The results from this investigation are in reasonably good agreement with their experimentally determined σ 3PA . We expect that in the future, our results for FP chromophores could be improved by the inclusion of effects of the protein, which are well-known to play important roles in determining the magnitude of 1PA, 2PA, and 3PA cross-sections. Finally, this investigation contributes to the understanding of multi-photon absorption photophysics of existent FPs and, furthermore, assists in the future engineering of new 3PA responsive FPs and FP chromophores.
items.authors: Maria Rossano-Tapia, Maryna Mondrusova, Ashton R. Henderson, Alex Brown

items.title: Adaptive Voiding Enables Interfacial Morphological Control at Low Stack Pressure in Solid-State Batteries
items.abstract: Solid-state batteries with alkali metal anodes offer high energy density and improved safety, but their performance is hindered by void formation at the metal-solid electrolyte interface during metal stripping, leading to impedance rise and increased probability of dendrite formation upon plating. Here, we demonstrate that low concentrations ( 5 vol%) of potassium metal added to industrial-grade lithium metal creates a dispersed Na-K liquid phase that suppresses voiding and enables stable, high-capacity stripping at practical current densities and stack pressures below 1 MPa. We furthermore identify a low-frequency oscillatory impedance attributed to “adaptive voiding”—the cyclic expansion and contraction of interfacial voids arising from an interplay between void growth and lithium deformation. This behavior, revealed by cryo-PFIB imaging and electrochemical analysis, offers a diagnostic signature for evaluating interfacial stability. These findings highlight new opportunities for designing robust, high-capacity SSBs operable under realistic mechanical constraints by controlling dynamic interfacial morphologies.
items.authors: Vijay D Veeraraghavan, Chiung-Yuan Lo, Andrew B Li, Sriram S Murali, Cole D Fincher, Hancheng Zhao

items.title: A Simple and Green One-Pot Synthesis of 2-Arylbenzimidazoles from Alcohols Using MnO2/I2
items.abstract: A straightforward and green synthetic method has been developed to prepare functionalized 2-arylbenzimidazole derivatives from readily accessible starting materials (arylmethyl alcohols and o-phenylenediamines) via a two-step, one-pot reaction. In the first step, arylmethyl alcohols are oxidized using MnO2 (4-8 equiv.) under both solvent-free and toluene-mediated conditions. subsequently, the aromatic aldehyde undergoes a 10 mol% iodine-catalyzed condensation with o-phenylenediamine in toluene at 100 °C under open-air conditions, leading to the production of 2-substituted benzimidazoles. The one-pot direct conversion of benzyl alcohols to 2-arylbenzimidazoles proceeds efficiently, affording the desired benzofused imidazoles in good to excellent yields, up to 91%. The sustainable method exhibits broad substrate scope, tolerating a wide range of functional groups. Mechanistic studies support a plausible imine formation pathway, followed by cyclization and oxidative aromatization under open-air conditions. This work highlights the synthetic utility and potential of the developed green method for future applications in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry.
items.authors: Savita Gat, Selvam Vasanth, Jayshree Nandkumar Solanke, Vasudevan Dhayalan, Rambabu Dandela

items.authors: Jakub Wagner, Eglė Tankelevičiūtė, Haoyang Li, Tomas Matulaitis, Maja Morawiak, Maciej Jelecki

items.title: Dearomative Multifunctionalization of Benzene Rings Enabled by Electron-Transfer Catalysis
items.abstract: Transforming simple benzene-ring-containing compounds from bulk chemicals into complex three-dimensional molecules with diverse functionalities and controllable stereochemistry under mild, scalable conditions remains a long-standing goal in synthetic chemistry. Dianions generated from aryl carbonyl compounds by two-electron transfer are promising precursors for dearomative difunctionalization. However, previous methods1 for generating dianion intermediates require harsh conditions and are incompatible with functionalized electrophiles, while competing benzylic functionalization via ketyl radical anions2,3 further limits their application. A key challenge is therefore to rapidly convert radical anions into higher-energy dianions using a mild reducing agent, outcompeting nucleophilic reactions of radical anions while ensuring electrophile compatibility. Here we report an ultrafast electron-transfer catalytic mode employing a bipyridine-based catalyst that rapidly acquires electrons from magnesium metal and transfers them to aryl ketyl radical anions, enabling the efficient in situ generation of dianion intermediates from simple aryl ketones under mild conditions. Using chlorosilanes as electrophiles, we obtain dearomatized bis-silylated products bearing conjugated enol silyl ether and allylsilane motifs in up to 98% yield. These products serve as versatile platform molecules for dearomative multifunctionalization, enabling the highly stereoselective synthesis of complex compounds with multiple stereocentres.
items.authors: Meng Li, Nan-Nan Li, Cai-Lan Kou, Zi-Yi Chen, Xi Luo, Jian-Bo Xie

items.title: Unlocking PEG-400: A Sustainable Reaction Medium for Phthalocyanine Synthesis and Pd-Catalyzed C–C Bond Formation
items.abstract: In this work, we demonstrate that poly(ethylene glycol)-400 (PEG-400) can efficiently replace conventional and hazardous solvents such as N,N-dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) in the synthesis of phthalocyanines, a class of functional molecular materials widely investigated for optoelectronic and energy-related applications. Used at a loading as low as 1.0 equivalent relative to the phthalonitrile precursor, PEG-400 enables cyclotetramerization reactions under operationally simple and comparatively safer conditions, providing isolated yields of 50-83% across a range of metalated and metal-free derivatives and substitution patterns. The robustness of the protocol was further demonstrated at the multigram scale, affording cobalt phthalocyanine in 79% yield, with 88% of the PEG-400 recovered from the reaction mixture. Remarkably, PEG-400 proved compatible with sequential cyclotetramerization followed by Sonogashira or Suzuki coupling without isolation of the macrocyclic intermediate, affording functionalized products in up to 75% yield and enabling pot-economical access to more complex derivatives. E-factor and Process Mass Intensity (PMI) analyses quantitatively support the improved material-efficiency profile of the method when compared to representative literature procedures. Overall, these results establish PEG-400 as a versatile and sustainable medium for the resource-efficient synthesis and functionalization of phthalocyanine derivatives.
items.authors: Federica Palmeri, Venanzio Raglione, Chiara Salvitti, Anna Troiani, Gloria Zanotti

items.title: Electrosynthesis of Bis-spirocycles via a Radical Strain-Release Dearomatization Cascade
items.abstract: This report presents an electro-oxidative approach to synthesize functionalized bis-spirocycles by combining the strain-release reactivity of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with arene dearomatization in a radical cascade. Various radical precursors can undergo this transformation under mild, oxidant- and mediator-free conditions, allowing efficient production of complex, three-dimensional bis-spirocyclic structures with high functional-group tolerance. Mechanistic investigations indicate an anodically driven radical cascade, involving radical addition to the BCB, strain-release ring opening, and subsequent ipso-dearomatization.
items.authors: Pooja Bhardwaj, Braja Kishor Paul, Padmanabha Samanta, Pintu Kumbhakar, Aritri Saha, Suman De Sarkar

items.title: Comprehensive Strategies in the Synthesis of Noncanonical Cyclic Peptides Containing Biaryl-Bridged Linkages
items.abstract: CONSPECTUS: The development of synthetic methodologies for natural products and the establishment of chemical supply routes for complex compounds, which advanced significantly in the twentieth century, provided organic chemists in both academia and industry with considerable confidence and assurance. These achievements offered humanity a systematic framework and a degree of sustainability in the supply of complex organic molecules. Established synthetic strategies enabled access, to a certain extent, to diverse bioactive compounds such as terpenes, alkaloids, and peptides. The isolation of bioactive natural products has often been compared to the extraction of crude oil, and we are repeatedly taught that the major bioactive natural products or their core scaffolds have already been “almost completely isolated.” Yet such a sense of accomplishment is frequently illusory. In reality, isolation techniques for bioactive natural products have advanced dramatically over time, and reports of newly isolated bioactive compounds continue to appear with vigor. In recent decades, the rapid progress of genome mining since the early 2000s has enabled the computational analysis of genetic information to uncover novel bioactive substances with pharmaceutical potential. This technology revealed that many organisms harbor, within their genomes, numerous beneficial bioactive compounds that are not produced under conventional environmental conditions. Consequently, a surge of discoveries—akin to a gold rush—has been reported. Among these natural products are compounds with previously unknown and distinctive scaffolds, many of which lack established synthetic supply routes. Notable examples include cihunamide B, lapparbin, micitide 982, rubrin, scabrirubin CB-4, and cyctetryptomycin A, all of which represent recently isolated noncanonical cyclic peptides characterized by biaryl-bridged linkages. Most of these compounds were discovered through genome mining and are distinguished by rigid architectures in which two aromatic rings, such as tryptophan and tyrosine, are covalently linked within the cyclic peptide framework. The presence of multiple highly conjugated sp2 carbons imparts pronounced linearity to the cyclic peptide backbone, concomitantly increasing structural strain. As a result, conventional strategies for cyclic peptide synthesis—such as intramolecular amide coupling, intramolecular Ullmann coupling, or intramolecular oxidative cyclization—are inadequate for constructing these highly strained biarylbridged cyclic peptides. We have recently established a general modular synthetic approach for these noncanonical cyclic peptides, enabling their supply on the gram scale. Most notably, this methodology not only permits the synthesis of naturally occurring biaryl-bridged linkages but also allows the deliberate incorporation of diverse, artificially designed aromatic motifs into arbitrary peptide linkers. Within the vast genetic “ocean” encoded in microbial genomes, numerous cryptic natural products with unprecedented scaffolds are expected to remain undiscovered. The systematic synthetic strategy we present herein provides a general and coherent framework that enables access to these compound classes, which until now have been exclusively available through microbial biosynthesis. Moreover, recent advances in photochemical and electrochemical methodologies, particularly inexpensive and mild radical reactions, have proven to be highly effective approaches for the synthesis of these previously unexplored natural products. These cutting-edge single-electron processes are not merely substitutes for classical two-electron name reactions; rather, they have emerged as powerful tools for navigating the genomic “ocean” and uncovering new chemical space.
items.authors: Hugh Nakamura

items.title: Synthetic Mutagenesis of Tyrosine into Proline Mimetics Enables Late-Stage Backbone Editing of Peptides
items.abstract: The biological and physicochemical properties of peptides are strongly influenced by their backbone conformations. However, installing conformationally restricting units generally requires peptide redesign and resynthesis using noncanonical amino acids. Here, we report a late-stage backbone-editing method that converts a native amino acid residue into a proline-mimetic structure. Treatment of the dearomatized intermediate generated by tyrosine-selective oxime conjugation in a basic aqueous buffer induced intramolecular 1,4-addition of the backbone amide nitrogen, thereby converting the tyrosine residue into a cyclic proline-mimetic unit within the peptide backbone. This transformation proceeded efficiently under mild aqueous conditions and was applicable to several bioactive peptides. Multidimensional NMR analyses established the structures of the resulting products, while conventional molecular dynamics and REST2 simulations demonstrated that the installed proline-mimetic backbone reduced the local conformational freedom of the peptide. Evaluation using a β-hairpin model peptide further demonstrated that the proline-mimetic structure enhanced resistance to proteolytic degradation. This method constitutes a chemical mutagenesis strategy that directly converts a native tyrosine residue into a backbone conformational control unit without reconstructing the parent peptide sequence. By connecting residue-selective side-chain modification with backbone editing, this strategy provides a new design concept for the late-stage conformational and functional diversification of peptides.
items.authors: Takaya Togo, Takumi Ueda, Yuko Otani, Yuka Furukawa, Kohei Nogita, Katsuya Maruyama

items.title: Diffusion-Model-Guided Adaptive Sampling of Rare Conformational States in Adenylate Kinase
items.abstract: Efficiently exploring the rare conformational states of biomolecules remains a central challenge in molecular dynamics simulation. Here we show, using adenylate kinase as a methodological testbed, that the static structural scores conventionally used to prioritize diffusion-modelgenerated candidates have essentially no power to predict which candidates actually reach a kinetically rare state upon subsequent simulation (AUC = 0.500, 95% CI [0.251, 0.749]). Motivated by this finding, we introduce two adaptive strategies — direct PCA-distance targeting and replication of confirmed-hit structures — that achieve significantly higher rare-state hit rates and dwell times than extended conventional molecular dynamics or random-initialization sampling under matched computational budgets, while also enabling, for the first time, statistically stable estimation of rare-macrostate populations. These results show that structural novelty and kinetically meaningful entry into a rare state are not the same property, providing concrete design guidance for generative-model-driven adaptive sampling in other biomolecular systems.
items.authors: Yoshitake Sakae

items.title: Comprehensive Chemical Space Exploration in De Novo Drug Design: An Algorithmically Constrained, Parallel Dual-Paradigm Framework Validated on BACE1
items.abstract: Isolated de novo drug design paradigms carry inherent vulnerabilities: ligand-based (LBDD) models risk unreliable extrapolation beyond their training domain, while structure-based (SBDD) genetic algorithms accumulate molecular size-bias across evolutionary generations. Furthermore, on structurally complex targets, deploying either paradigm in isolation risks systematically excluding viable chemical space. Here, we introduce a dual-paradigm framework addressing both failure modes through two novel algorithmic constraints: a Zoned Applicability Domain (AD) integrated as a live reinforcement learning reward gradient, and the Size-Independent Ligand Efficiency (SILE) metric deployed as a generational fitness function. A convergent validation cascade - pharmacokinetic filtering, exhaustive docking, and molecular dynamics - is architecturally positioned to eliminate artifacts these constrained engines may still produce. We evaluated this workflow on β-secretase (BACE1), deliberately selected because its electrostatic catalytic dyad and hydrophobic sub-pockets present divergent reward landscapes. Ablation studies confirmed the Zoned AD suppressed out-of-domain artifacts to enrich extrapolation, while SILE prevented meaningless molecular bloat compared to baseline models. The LBDD pipeline autonomously rediscovered 10 withheld experimental inhibitors, while the SBDD pipeline successfully decoupled docking affinity from molecular size, with both yielding leads with thermodynamic profiles comparable to the clinical reference verubecestat. Critically, the campaign demonstrated a fundamental algorithmic divergence: LBDD generates data-driven compounds inheriting the binding topology of known inhibitors, while SBDD explores pocket-complementary space with substantially different binding mechanisms. This suggests that parallel deployment of constrained paradigms may be necessary for systematic coverage of a target's viable binding space.
items.authors: Thang T. Dang, Mai N. Luong

items.title: Rapid, Reliable and Accurate XPS Depth-Distribution Functions from the Berger–Doggett method
items.abstract: Two complementary rapid Monte Carlo methods for emission-depth distributions were introduced for Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in 1993; the statistical weights method and the Berger-Doggett method. The statistical-weights method samples both elastic scattering directions and the distances between elastic events; the Berger–Doggett method conditions on the angular history and analytically averages over all such distances. These were much faster (by orders of magnitude) than previous methods and no less accurate. Besides reducing variance, the two methods should provide an unusually strong independent cross-check in their common domain of a homogeneous sample. As computer resources have progressively increased over the last 30 years, longer Monte Carlo runs have become practical, and in those a numerical instability can arise in the Berger-Doggett approach that we solve in this paper. We reformulate the original integral recurrence as a lower-bidiagonal system of linear ordinary differential equations with mixed boundary conditions. An ordered Schur decomposition selects the bounded invariant subspace and the required fluences are obtained from the action of a matrix exponential, avoiding the chance near-co-linear direction cosines that would occasionally frustrate the method published in 1993, and now allows very long Monte-Carlo runs to be performed quickly and reliably. In controlled tests the original method accumulated a relative error of 7.6 × 1010 at a cosine separation of 10−14, whereas the new formulation remained within 2.3 × 10−16 of a 120-digit reference. In a 500 angle-history recalculation using contemporary NIST SRD 64 elastic data, at a typical C 1s kinetic energy the old method gave a relative error of 6.2 × 1012 in the coefficient recurrence even though its closest pair of direction cosines differed by 1.15 × 10−4; the new formulation agreed with a 160-digit result to 1.6 × 10−16. This removes the need for extended or arbitrary precision without changing the underlying transport model. Routine Berger-Doggett calculations can now be done on a typical PC reliably and almost instantly, supporting also the statistical weights method by making it easier to verify implementations of it. This should be a significant step towards the automated extraction of all the information possible from nondestructive XPS depth-profiling. As an example of its wide applicability, the calculation confirms the physical basis of a previously proposed coaxial XPS geometry, producing a depth-distribution function with a subsurface maximum. Its considerable breadth, however, suggests enhanced subsurface selectivity rather than any general resolution of the ill-conditioning of depth-profile reconstruction.
items.authors: Peter J. Cumpson

items.title: Aqueous Crystallization Unlocks Tunable Structural Color from Isoxanthopterin
items.abstract: In nature, some animals generate reflective tissues through the controlled precipitation of organic matter. Whether assembled as amorphous structures within the lumen of butterfly wing scales to produce color, or as spherulitic nanomaterials within the epithelial cells of certain vertebrates and crustaceans to enhance visual acuity, certain biomolecules exhibit a conserved capacity to template structures whose refractive index and morphology directly govern optical properties. One such example, isoxanthopterin, produces some of the most reflective structures found in biology yet remains largely unexplored as an engineered material, owing in part to its limited solubility. We investigate the chemical principles underlying isoxanthopterin assembly in aqueous solution and show that the balance between electrostatic repulsion and hydrogen bonding governs crystal formation, with pH tuning this balance to modulate size and, in turn, bulk optical properties. These structural and optical differences reveal simple design principles for engineering color from a single starting biomolecule, informing the design of future aqueous-based optical materials
items.authors: Wen Dou, Leila F. Deravi

items.title: A tertiary network couples hydrophobic substitutions to terminal contacts in an IDP
items.abstract: Conformational ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are sensitive to changes in amino acid sequence. Even chemically conservative substitutions can alter global properties and interactions far from the mutation site, but how these effects propagate across the sequence remains unclear. Here, we investigated six chemically conservative substitutions at site 66, in addition to the naturally occurring Val66 sequence of the intrinsically disordered Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) prodomain to understand how a substitution near the center of the sequence affects the termini. Using 896 µs of all-atom explicit-solvent enhanced molecular dynamics simulations and Blobulation, we find that each substitution affects ensemble compactness, which was reflected in contacts between the terminal hydrophobic blobs. For five of the seven sequences, we identified contact associations consistent with an indirect pathway connecting the mutation site to the termini through an intermediate hydrophobic blob. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how chemically conservative substitutions produce sequence-dependent changes in IDP ensembles and establish an approach for identifying direct and indirect interaction pathways through which the effects of a mutation propagate.
items.authors: Lindsey M. Riggs, Ruchi Lohia, Grace Brannigan

items.title: Engineering chirality in threaded BODIPYs
items.abstract: In this article, we explore the possibility of introducing chirality at different structural levels within boron-threaded BODIPYs. Three strategies were investigated, involving a chiral macrocycle, a stereogenic boron center and an axially chiral BODIPY dimer. In the latter case, double threading through boron coordination was achieved for the first time. The optical and chiroptical properties of the three chiral systems were investigated. While the chiral macrocycle leads to the most pronounced chiroptical response with clear evidence of chirality transfer to the BODIPY, all three architectures display measurable electronic circular dichroism and circularly polarized luminescence. These results demonstrate that chirality can be deliberately positioned at distinct structural levels of threaded BODIPYs, providing a modular platform to investigate the interplay between molecular architecture and chiroptical properties.
items.authors: Matthieu Hicguet, Maher Hojorat, Maxime Lebreton, Nicolas Vanthuyne, Ludovic Favereau, Fabienne Berrée

items.title: Integrating Theory–Experiment Active Learning and Mechanistic Insights for High-Entropy Alloy Design Toward Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
items.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) offer diverse local coordination environments for modulating hydrogen adsorption and water activation in alkaline hydrogen evolution, but their highdimensional compositional space remains difficult to explore efficiently. Theory-experiment closed loops can accelerate this search, yet theoretical prior and candidate sampling are commonly coupled, obscuring their individual contributions. Here, we developed a theory-experiment activelearning (TEA) framework that independently varies theoretical priors and candidate sampling strategies for AuCuPdPtIr HEAs. Under identical experimental throughput, the theoretical prior provided transferable performance trends across composition space, whereas the proposed adaptive sampling strategy broadened effective compositional coverage. After three iterations involving 120 compositions, the framework identified Au16Cu5Pd35Pt35Ir9, which required only 16 mV overpotential to reach 10 mA cm-2 in 1 M KOH. An anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) cell using this catalyst as the cathode reached 1 A cm-2 at 1.647 V and 60 °C and operated stably for 1000 h. Model interpretation, operando infrared spectroscopy, machine-learning-potential molecular dynamics (MLP-MD) simulations, and charge-density analysis further associated Ir/Cu-related local environments with a weaker interfacial hydrogenbond network and more Volmer-like water configurations. This work connects controlled module comparison, data-efficient compositional optimization, and interfacial-water mechanisms, providing a general strategy for complex multicomponent electrocatalysts.
items.authors: Jinpeng Li, Baicheng Zhang, Zongzi Jin, Man Luo, Zixu Sun, Conghui Li

items.title: van der Waals-Guided Nanopatterning Perovskite Nanocrystal Superlattices for Active Light-Emitting Metasurfaces
items.abstract: High-resolution nanopatterning of self-assembled colloidal nanocrystal superlattices is crucial for their integration into miniaturized devices and integrated photonics. However, conventional top-down lithography often compromises supercrystallinity and dissolves constituent nanocrystals. Here, we introduce a non-destructive, bottom-up approach for the site-specific nucleation and growth of perovskite superlattices. Guided by the Lifshitz theory of van der Waals forces, we engineer a sharp permittivity contrast within nanotemplates to manipulate localized dewetting dynamics. This tailored interaction landscape establishes deep thermodynamic sinks that selectively drive the site-specific nucleation of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals. Corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations, we reveal that these dynamic energy sinks strictly restrict the rotational degrees of freedom of incoming nanocrystals, ultimately promoting highly ordered, face-to-face superlattice packing. This approach yields uniform, large-area arrays with subwavelength feature sizes and periodicities down to 200 and 350 nanometers, respectively, achieving an unprecedented array density exceeding 8 x 106 mm-2. Deterministic control over superlattice dimensions and array periodicity enables precise momentum-space engineering of radiation patterns, realizing highly directional light-emitting metasurfaces with an ultranarrow beam divergence of only 8.5°. Finally, we demonstrate the monolithic integration of these arrays into subwavelength electrically-driven active light-emitting metasurfaces, unlocking robust on-chip light modulation. This work establishes a robust pathway for translating the extraordinary properties of perovskite superlattices into next-generation on-chip nanophotonics.
items.authors: Donato Maria Carretta, Zhan-Hong Lin, Gianluca Vagli, Sunil B. Shivarudraiah, Jiwoo Oh, Abhijit Gogoi

items.title: Tetraethylammonium Cations Enable C2+ Product Formation in Acidic CO2 Reduction
items.abstract: Cation effect is essential to obtain selectivity towards carbon dioxide (CO 2 )​ reduction reaction (CO 2 ​RR) over the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media. Selectivity towards CO 2 RR has been largely attributed to the coordination between alkali cations and CO 2 -derived intermediates. Here, we provide a different perspective by demonstrating that tetraethylammonium (Et 4 ​N + ), a weakly coordinating cation, can also effectively suppress the HER in acidic media, favoring CO 2 ​RR on both Ag and Cu electrodes. The generation of both C 1 ​ and C 2+ ​ products on Cu indicates that the direct participation of alkali cations as co-catalyst is not a prerequisite for CO 2 activation or C-C coupling. We find that CO 2 ​RR is independent of the bulk pH in the presence of 1 M Et 4 ​N + , as evidenced by similar selectivity across acidic, neutral, and alkaline media. In addition, rigorous impurities control reveals that millimolar-levels of triethylammonium chloride (Et 3 ​NHCl) substantially promote HER on Cu catalyst, hence calling for careful impurity control. Overall, this work reveals the use of Et 4 ​N + as an valuable platform to investigate the effects of cations or impurities for CO 2 ​RR.
items.authors: Damien Degoulange, Qiucheng Xu, Miyeon Chang, Wenchao Ma, Jacobus C. Duburg, Xile Hu

items.title: Connected, but for how long? A residual-lifetime criterion for the hydraulic–diffusive boundary in polyamide reverse-osmosis membranes
items.abstract: The mechanism of water transport through the polyamide active layer of reverse-osmosis membranes is again contested: a 2023 claim that transport is governed by pore flow rather than solution-diffusion reopened a debate many considered settled, and a two-phase treatment has since shown the two descriptions are not mutually exclusive once their coefficients are matched. That reconciliation, however, answers a phenomenological question, not a structural one: whether a genuine, pressure-bearing continuous water phase exists is a separate, testable claim about the material. This Perspective argues that settling it requires two conditions prior work has largely treated as one — an instantaneous through-connected topology, and its survival over the transport timescale — and that the second condition has so far been estimated the wrong way: from the total lifetime of a connectivity interval rather than the residual lifetime seen by a water molecule arriving at a random instant, the same statistical root as the inspection paradox. A dynamic accessibility measure, Adyn = θ·SR(τtr), is proposed to close this gap, built on an intensive areal connectivity measure θ and a residual-lifetime survival function SR rather than an assumed exponential decay. A minimal structural surrogate places the connectivity transition at a model water-accessible volume fraction of 0.14–0.17, close to atomistic estimates for real polyamide, and a comparison of accessible simulation timescales with the residence time implied by realistic operating conditions shows why molecular dynamics alone cannot currently resolve the question. A concrete, falsifiable test agenda is proposed.
items.authors: Ye. O. Kolomiiets, Yevhen Kolomiiets

items.title: Subtle differences in interlayer energetics dictate facet-dependent elastic and plastic flexibility in a molecular crystal
items.abstract: Mechanically flexible molecular crystals hold promise for emerging functional materials such as optoelectronics and piezoelectrics. Here, we report a rare example of facet-dependent elastic and plastic bending in a molecular crystal. Synchrotron micro-focused X-ray diffraction mapping (µ-XRD) and X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr) reveal distinct domain-level structural changes during plastic versus elastic deformation and variations in intermolecular interactions across the slip planes that govern these distinct mechanical responses. Potential energy densities evaluated at the interaction regions from QCr models, along with the subtle difference in interlayer binding energies (ΔE = 2.2 kJ mol-1) reveal more robust interactions that underpin the elastically bending facet. µ-XRD mapping uncovers the atomistic origin of elastic deformation in terms of molecular reorientation (Δθ = 0.38°) and packing density gradients in the bent region, whereas plastic deformation proceeds via irreversible molecular slippage, quantified by a 5-fold increase in crystal mosaicity (from 0.06° to 0.30°). These findings correlate subtle electron-density and energetic features with the domain-level changes underlying this rare phenomenon.
items.authors: Atiqur Rahman, Ravi Teja Malisetty, Amit K. Pradhan, Aditya K. Prajapati, Vivian G. Shang, John C. McMurtrie

items.title: Origin of the Exceptional Activity in Molybdenum-Catalysed Dinitrogen Reduction with Samarium Diiodide and Water
items.abstract: Molybdenum complexes supported by phosphine–ligand–phosphine (PLP) pincers, combined with samarium diiodide and water, convert dinitrogen to ammonia under mild conditions with nitrogenase-like activities. Using explicitly correlated coupled-cluster calculations, spin–orbit corrections, and realistic concentration and speciation models, we elucidate the cleavage mechanism from N 2 -bound Mo(I) complexes to ammonia release. Dimerisation proceeds through pentacoordinate Mo(I)–N 2 complexes, and N 2 activation is controlled by terminal N 2 dissociation, which converts a [Mo]–N≡N–[Mo] unit into cleavage-ready [Mo]=N=N=[Mo] before spin crossover and bond scission. The resulting nitrido intermediates are reduced by outer-sphere, Sm-mediated concerted proton-coupled electron transfer (cPCET). This pathway avoids the high-energy charge-separated intermediates of stepwise PT/ET and the loss of strong azaphilic Sm(III)–N interactions upon Sm–OH formation in inner-sphere alternatives. Aggregation into ammonia-binding Sm(III) hydroxide oligomers and precipitation stabilise the product states and render reduction effectively irreversible. These features explain the exceptional activity of Mo/SmI 2 /H 2 O systems. The first cPCET is rate-determining under typical conditions, whereas N 2 activation becomes limiting at low catalyst concentrations or with electron-withdrawing ligands. Pincer geometry and π-acidity facilitate cPCET, but efficient catalysis requires ligands that avoid over-stabilising low Mo oxidation states during N 2 activation while accommodating changing coordination numbers across the cycle.
items.authors: Jonas Himmelstrup, Leif E. Hertwig, Vidar Remi Jensen

items.title: Metabolic Competition Reshapes the Performance of Engineered Polyketide Synthases
items.abstract: Directed evolution is widely used to enhance enzymatic performance and evolve new-to-nature reactivities, typically in vitro or in model microbial systems. However, variants selected in a model host may not retain their relative performance in the intended production organism. Here, we engineered a single 2-pyrone synthase (2PS) scaffold by directed evolution in Escherichia coli ( E. coli ) and evaluated the resulting variants in both E. coli and planta. In E. coli, engineered 2PS variants showed distinct chemoselectivities, giving access to precursors for kavalactones and raspberry ketone from one protein scaffold. The best variant achieved 98% conversion of p -coumaric acid to 200 µg/mL bisnoryangonin. In planta, however, variant performance was reordered: the top-performing microbial variant was outperformed 2.7-fold by one with lower activity in E. coli . We traced this host-dependent shift to competition for the shared p -coumaroyl-CoA pool and identified cinnamoyl-CoA reductase from Nicotiana benthamiana ( Nb CCR) as a key competing enzyme. Introducing Nb CCR into E. coli recapitulated the variant rank order observed in planta, demonstrating that metabolic competition can reshape the performance of engineered enzymes across hosts. These results also suggest that reconstructing key competing pathways of the target host in a tractable microbial system can provide a practical strategy for engineering enzymes for otherwise difficult-to-evolve production hosts. Finally, 2PS variants enabled the chemoenzymatic synthesis of natural and fluorinated kavalactones with up to 64% isolated yield over two steps.
items.authors: Yu Zhou, Zhengyao Shao, Xueyi Xue, Li-Qing Chen, Hong Qiao, Yi Lu

items.title: A scalable framework for goal-driven task-based simulations
items.abstract: Realistic surfaces of active materials that involve the motion of atoms or ions in their function typically change their (sub-)surface composition and geometry under operating conditions due to varying environmental stimuli, degradation or healing processes, but also just while exhibiting their intended function, making it difficult to build simulation models that remain valid as the system evolves. Such problems often demand large-scale computation together with efficient data processing, so scalable task execution and data-efficient synchronization become critical. We present a scalable computational framework that supports large collections of independent computation tasks with incremental result aggregation. We demonstrate the framework using adaptive kinetic Monte Carlo (akMC) as a showcase application, where transition-state searches are performed on-the-fly. The new framework employs a hierarchical orchestrator–worker architecture implemented with modern MPI constructs and operates efficiently from single workstations to multi-node high-performance computing systems. It integrates well-established simulation engines such as LAMMPS and supports multi-core CPU and GPU parallelism within each task. Performance is demonstrated using classical, machine-learning, and GPU-accelerated interatomic potentials. Benchmarks show strong scaling across multiple compute nodes with several hundreds of CPU-cores, efficient utilization of multi-core executors and GPU sharing. The results indicate that the framework provides an efficient solution for rare-event and mesoscopic simulation workflows.
items.authors: Carlos Lopez, King Chun Lai, Markus Rampp, Christoph Scheurer

items.title: Intelligent Microscopy for Materials: Leakage-Controlled SEM Morphology Classification with Calibration, Explainability, and Artifact Perturbation
items.abstract: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image classification is increasingly used to organize large microscopy archives, but high predictive accuracy alone does not establish that a model is scientifically reliable. Duplicate images, class imbalance, acquisition annotations, poorly calibrated confidence, and post hoc use of test data can all make performance appear stronger than it is. This study develops a leakage-controlled and reliability oriented workflow for ten-class SEM morphology classification using the public NFFA-EUROPE 100% SEM Dataset v2.0. The 21,169 source images were audited before modelling. Full-file MD5 screening removed 332 exact duplicates,while a perceptual-hash/structural-similarity pipeline identified 92 high-confidence near duplicate groups and removed 95 additional redundant images, producing a final modelling cohort of 20,742 images. A single stratified 70/15/15 train/validation/test split was then frozen for all experiments. Three model families were evaluated under this protocol: a1,041-feature hand crafted image descriptor with classical machine learning, a convolutional neural network trained from scratch,and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18. On the held-out test set, the selected ResNet-18 achieved 0.942802 accuracy, 0.930980 balanced accuracy,and 0.931633 macro-F1, compared with 0.7789/0.6713/0.6890 for the classical baseline and 0.7947/0.8421/0.7425 for the scratch CNN.Validation-fitted temperature scaling reduced test expected calibration error from 0.018974 to 0.011369 without changing predicted classes. Grad-CAM provided coarse spatial checks of model attention, while a controlled chromatic-annotation-region perturbation experiment showed a larger mean absolute class-probability change than equal-area translated controls (0.032554 vs 0.002420; Wilcoxon p = 1.07 x 10^-26), but only 4 of 172 targeted images changed predicted class. Selective prediction further increased retained-image accuracy to 0.980007 at approximately 90% coverage while rejecting 68.54% of all test errors. Together, these results support a predominantly morphology-driven transfer model with measurable localized artifact sensitivity and show how dataset integrity, calibration, perturbation analysis, and confidence-based review can complement headline accuracy in materials microscopy.
items.authors: Dennis Obinna Orji

items.title: Immunometabolic Signaling Networks in HIV Persistence: From Cellular Metabolism to Reservoir Control
items.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) successfully suppresses systemic HIV-1 replication, yet latent reservoirs persist in long-lived memory CD4+ T cells, myeloid lineages, and specialized anatomical sanctuaries. While previous immunometabolic studies have documented altered bioenergetic profiles in infected host cells, the upstream signaling mechanisms that govern these metabolic states and drive viral fate remain incompletely defined. Here, we present a comprehensive framework positioning intracellular immunometabolic signaling networks—specifically PI3K–AKT–mTOR, AMPK, and HIF-1α—as central transducers linking extracellular microenvironmental signals to cellular bioenergetics, epigenetic remodeling, and viral persistence. We evaluate how the interplay between mTOR-, AMPK-, and HIF-1α-associated signaling influences metabolic and transcriptional states that may shape the balance between active viral expression and deep transcriptional latency. Furthermore, we examine how oxygen-sensing through HIF-1α, tissue-specific nutrient microenvironments (in GALT, lymph nodes, and the CNS), and mitochondrial ROS signaling shape reservoir longevity, clonal expansion, and resistance to apoptosis. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies, contrasting traditional "shock and kill" approaches with "metabolically reprogram and kill" modalities designed to lower the threshold for latency reversal. Understanding and therapeutically manipulating the signaling–metabolism–latency axis may provide new strategies for disrupting viral reservoirs and promoting durable HIV remission.
items.authors: Samuel Long, Abigail Long

items.title: Nonlinear Optical Response in Water-Soluble Ionic Carbon Nitride Photocatalysts: A Two-Photon Absorption Study
items.abstract: The two-photon absorption in water-soluble ionic PHI photocatalysts is investigated by single-beam z-scan. A systematic variation of sample concentration and laser irradiance shows that nonlinear absorption in the material is governed by trap states, the nature of which is controlled by the type of cation.
items.authors: Nikita Vashistha, Arindam Konar, Johannes Liessem, Radim Beranek, Benjamin Dietzek-Ivanšić

items.title: Understanding and quantifying interfacial ion exchange in hybrid electrolytes
items.abstract: In pursuit of practical solid-state lithium batteries with low cost and scalable manufacturing, hybrid electrolytes that combine Li + -conducting inorganic electrolyte particles with liquid or polymer electrolytes have emerged as a promising strategy. 1-2 In these systems, Li + needs to transport through the interface between the percolating organic electrolyte matrix and the dispersed inorganic particles. However, interfacial Li + transport dynamics remain poorly understood largely due to lack of reliable experimental measurements. 3-4 Here, we introduce two straightforward nuclear magnetic resonance techniques − spin saturation transfer and selective inversion-recovery − to directly and unambiguously quantify Li + exchange in hybrid electrolytes. This enables us to build a new theoretical framework based on the exchange kinetics to analyze Li + transport in organic-inorganic hybrid electrolytes. By studying several representative hybrid electrolytes, we demonstrate that the ratio of inorganic particle radius and ionic Kapitza length predicts whether the incorporation of Li + -conducting particles into organic electrolytes will lead to hybrid electrolytes with improved conductivity. This study thus provides quantitative measurements and physical scaling principles to systematically design hybrid electrolytes for solid-state batteries.
items.authors: Deyang Yu, Bryan D. McCloskey, Rui Qiao, Louis A. Madsen

items.title: In Situ and Operando Neutron Powder Diffraction of NaxNiO2: a Case Study for Sodium-ion Batteries
items.abstract: Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) is a non-destructive technique uniquely suited to investigating industrially relevant sodium-ion cathode materials. Unlike X-ray diffraction, it offers excellent contrast between neighbouring transition metal ions and is sensitive to lighter elements such as O/Na, which are key to revealing superstructural orderings characteristic of sodium cathodes. However, in situ/operando NPD battery studies are hindered by sample quantity requirements, and lack of suitable sample environments. Using a cell developed at ISIS Neutron and Muon Source, we observed no detrimental effects from prolonged vacuum exposure required for Time-of-Flight NPD. We collect/analyse data in two modes: operando, in which the electrochemical structural evolution is tracked, and in situ, wherein higher signalto-noise data is collected during voltage holds, for phase-pure samples at set voltage cutoffs. Using Na x NiO 2 as a model system, we present a methodology to account for the complex background profile characteristic of electrochemical environments enabling, for the first time, quantitative Rietveld refinements against in situ electrochemical NPD, and providing a systematic framework for future studies. Structural models are refined against in situ data and benchmarked against combined refinement of ex situ SXRD/NPD measurements. This work unlocks potential for previously inaccessible insights into structure-property relationships and degradation, helping to facilitate the development of next-generation cathodes with enhanced useful lifetime, capacity, and performance.
items.authors: James M. A. Steele, Gabriel E. Pérez, Farheen N. Sayed, Liam A. V. Nagle-Cocco, Camilla Tacconis, Aurelio Lencioni

items.title: Structural characterization of fully chemically modified siRNA with lipid conjugate and divalent architecture
items.abstract: The development of delivery platforms, including lipid conjugates and multivalent scaffolds, has accelerated the emergence of extrahepatic-targeting small interfering RNA (siRNA). These molecular architectures have advanced multiple clinical-stage siRNA candidates targeting the central nervous system (CNS) and other extrahepatic tissues, underscoring an urgent need for analytical methodologies capable of resolving conjugate-derived fragmentation pathways and symmetric multivalent structures that complicate their characterization by tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS). Here, we develop complementary MS/MS and data-interpretation strategies for structural characterization of lipid-conjugated and fully chemically modified divalent siRNA using ion-pair-free hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC). Conjugate-derived fragmentation pathways were first established using a lipid-conjugated oligonucleotide standard via collision-induced dissociation (CID), higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD), and ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD), and the resulting framework was then applied to characterize a human Huntingtin (HTT)-targeting lipid-conjugated siRNA. For analysis of a symmetric divalent siRNA, a customized terminal fragment-based data-processing strategy was developed that preserved the complete molecular architecture and enabled assignment of terminal fragment ions from both halves of the construct without relying on internal fragments. This workflow provided comprehensive sequence characterization of divalent siRNA while substantially improving recovery of informative 3ʹ-terminal fragment ions compared with the conventional static 3ʹ-modification method. Collectively, the lipid-fragmentation framework and terminal fragment-based interpretation approach provided a robust analytical platform for structural characterization of increasingly complex conjugated and multivalent RNA therapeutics.
items.authors: Mohamed I. Gadallah, Noha M El Zahar, Thanh Nguyen, Kailyn L. Nonhof, Nicholas McHugh, Ken Yamada

items.title: Nitroarylphosphines: An Overlooked Family of Ligands
items.abstract: Homoleptic tris(nitroaryl)phoshines are very rare, “explosive-looking” molecules that have until now never been fully characterized. We show that they are accessible from nitroarylphosphine oxides and are, perhaps surprisingly, sufficiently thermally stable to be handled at ambient temperature and used as ligands. We show experimentally and computationally that they display significantly modulated electronic properties and we demonstrate several examples of their coordination complexes, thus showing the nitro group is an overlooked tuning tool in phosphine coordination chemistry.
items.authors: Rafael Pérez, Jean-Wilfrid Hayes Perreault, Guillaume Bélanger-Chabot

items.title: Linking electronic and geometrical structure to local magnetism in lanthanide hexacyanoferrates by paramagnetic solid-state NMR
items.abstract: Lanthanide hexacyanoferrates, LnFe(CN)6·xH2O, combine the structural versatility of cyanidebridged frameworks with the strong spin–orbit coupling and crystal-field effects of lanthanide ions. Yet, the local (ion-specific) origins of the magnetic response of these materials remain difficult to resolve by conventional solid-state chemistry techniques. Here, we report the 1H and 13C solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra of LnFe(CN)6·xH2O (Ln = La to Yb), with assignments supported by first-principles calculations and optical spectroscopy. We interpret the 1H NMR spectra in terms of free (interstitial) and bound (Ln-coordinated) water environments within the porous framework. The 1H shifts and shift anisotropies scale approximately linearly with the lanthanide Bleaney coefficients, establishing a direct and quantifiable link between 1H spectra and single-ion anisotropy. Using 13C NMR spectra, we are able to isolate the impact of Ln composition, despite the Ln contribution comprising only a small fraction (up to 3%) of the total paramagnetic NMR shift. The 13C shift anisotropy also tracks linearly with the Bleaney coefficients, whilst the trend against the isotropic shift is weaker, underlining the site-specific effect of Fermi contact and dipolar contributions to the total shift. Together, out results establish solid-state NMR spectroscopy as a sensitive and quantitative probe of single-ion anisotropy in cyanide-based frameworks.
items.authors: Wassilios Papawassiliou, Gabriel Balavoine, Euan N. Bassey, Ntaniela Kalemai, Nikolia Lalioti, Andrew J. Pell

items.title: Use of Gas Chromatography, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and Fluorescent methods to Estimate Enantiomeric Excess in Asymmetric Transfer Hydrogenation.
items.abstract: The use of Gas Chromatography, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and fluorescent methods to estimate ee are described, using asymmetric transfer hydrogenation (ATH) of acetophenone derivatives as a platform for the methodology. The use of rapid analysis processes may facilitate the screening samples through a simple process without having to use chiral HPLC or GC when generating an approximation of enantioselectivity.
items.authors: Michael Chu, Shiyun Chen, Thomas H. Hall, Roy Hodgkinson, David Robson, Robert Messias

items.title: There is no knee in Ragone: clarifying battery energy and power fade using Ragone plots
items.abstract: Ragone plots provide a compact representation of energy storage performance by relating accessible energy to power. Despite this, battery degradation is often described using simplified metrics such as “energy fade” and “power fade”, which obscure changes in the overall performance envelope. Here, we propose a shift towards a Ragone-based analysis of degradation, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of battery health. We use physics-based models to simulate ageing under a range of operating conditions and degradation modes, and evaluate Ragone plots over the course of ageing. Each degradation mechanism leaves a distinct signature in the Ragone plots, which can be directly associated with energy and power fade, as well as with specific internal states of the battery. We also show that the widely reported “knee” in reference performance tests is an artefact of testing protocols, rather than an intrinsic feature of battery behaviour, underscoring the advantages of Ragone-based characterisation. Finally, we introduce a systematic empirical method to extract energy and power fade from Ragone plots. These results demonstrate that Ragone analysis provides a more powerful framework for diagnosing, interpreting, and ultimately mitigating battery degradation in practical applications.
items.authors: Ferran Brosa Planella, Samuel J. Cooper

items.title: Do crown ethers fully dissociate ion pairs in aqueous solution?
items.abstract: In alkali fluoride solutions, crown ethers are widely assumed to generate "naked" anions by capturing cations, yet direct evidence for complete ion-pair dissociation is limited. We combine 19F Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) and multiscale modeling on aqueous NaF and KF with 18crown-6 (18C6). Fluoride diffusion slows on crown addition, scaling linearly with the crownbound cation fraction across both salts and extrapolating to zero without complexation. The 19F chemical shifts independently establish this retained ion pairing. For KF, the signal moves away from the free-ion baseline, the wrong direction for liberation. While NaF responds more weakly, the theoretical chemical shift profile shows that the crown-bound cation carries a shielding contact (CIP) region and a deshielding solvent-shared (SIP) region whose cancellation flattens the response. Molecular dynamics confirm reduced but persistent contact pairing. Crown ethers thus suppress contact pairing while retaining both solvent-shared and residual contact associations with the sequestered cation.
items.authors: Malgorzata Musial, Christopher L. Suiter, Jason Widegren, Demian Riccardi

items.title: Targeted mitigation strategies for critically polluted PM2.5 regions in India using spatially constrained airsheds
items.abstract: Air pollution in India is a regional problem, yet the current air quality management policy is largely city-centric. Here, we developed an airshed management framework that emphasizes cooperative action for PM2.5 pollution mitigation. This framework identifies air pollution control areas (APCAs) for targeted emissions control across four critically polluted regions in the Indo-Gangetic Plain by mapping sectoral emissions from administrative units to pollution levels to meet specified air quality targets. We find that the dominant emission sectors differ across APCAs, such as agriculture, transport, and domestic to micro, small and medium-scale industry, highlighting the inadequacy of broad regional airshed management and the need for tailored air quality management plans. This framework yields differentiated policy guidance at the airshed and sub-airshed scales for the districts that constitute an APCA, leading to a spatially fine-tuned and implicitly minimal-effort mitigation plan. The developed framework is generalizable worldwide to polluted regions at any PM2.5 level.
items.authors: Neeldip Barman, Lucas Rojas-Mendoza, Yuzhou Wang, Zainab Arub, Shivam Saxena, Piyush Bhardwaj

items.title: Influence of Non-Polar Amino Acids on the Phase Transitions of Atmospheric Aerosol Particles
items.abstract: The fate of aerosol particles in the atmosphere depends in part on their composition, morphology, and phase transitions. Studies of aerosol phase transitions have focused on aerosol particles with organic compounds consisting of C, H, and O atoms, although a substantial fraction of organic compounds contain heteroatoms such as sulfur and nitrogen. In this study, non-polar amino acids were used to study the effect of organonitrogen compounds on the phase transitions of droplets using optical microscopy. The ternary internal mixtures used were composed of ammonium sulfate (AS), a non-polar amino acid, and either 2-methylglutaric acid (2MGA) or 1,2,6-hexanetriol (126HT) (model oxidized organic compounds). The morphology, phase transitions, and spatially resolved chemical composition were characterized using optical and Raman microscopies. A suppression of the separation relative humidity was observed when the concentration of amino acid was more than 50% of the organic compound by weight. For some systems, the amino acid crystallizes, while the oxidized organic compounds and ammonium sulfate undergo liquid-liquid phase separation, yielding a three-phase system. Trends in the efflorescence relative humidity depend on the solubility of the amino acid. These studies are important in understanding the impact of organic-organic interactions as well as organonitrogen compounds on the phase transitions of aerosol particles, which have consequences for heterogeneous chemistry and cloud droplet nucleation in the atmosphere.
items.authors: Kiran Reddy Pitta, Kayla N. McCreary, Nahin Ferdousi-Rokib, Timothy M. Raymond, Dabrina D Dutcher, Akua A. Asa-Awuku

items.title: Concise Total Synthesis of (–)-5-epi-Cycloclavine via Metal- and Base-Free Diastereoselective
items.abstract: A metal- and base-free intramolecular cyclopropanation based on nonstabilized donor carbenes generated in situ from N-sulfonylhydrazones has been developed, enabling the construction of the highly strained aza[3.1.0]bicyclic core of (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine with concomitant complete stereocontrol of two all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. Combined with the straightforward introduction of methacrylic acid as four-carbon fragment from readily available enantiopure functionalized tricyclic indole derivative (4-amino Uhle's ketone), this strategy enabled a concise diasteroselective synthesis of the five-fused rings system present in (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine.
items.authors: Francesca Diotallevi, Francesca Bartoccini, Giovanni Piersanti

items.title: Molecular rotor-regulated target-selective photoinactivation of myostatin
items.abstract: Photoinactivation allows precise spatiotemporal control of biomolecules in biological systems. Among the photoinactivation strategies, photooxygenation is advantageous, as it can be readily induced with a photosensitizer upon photoirradiation in biological environment.
