However, its utility is limited by poor target selectivity arising from the excessive generation and high reactivity of reactive oxygen species. Here, target-selective photoinactivation of myostatin is achieved using a target-binding ligand functionalized with a molecular rotor-based photosensitizing unit whose photooxygenation activity is enhanced upon binding to the target protein. A novel molecular rotor-based photosensitizer was developed and conjugated to a myostatin-binding peptide. The resulting functionalized peptide selectively oxygenated and inactivated myostatin under near-infrared irradiation. Treatment with the peptide followed by irradiation decreased endogenous myostatin levels in skeletal muscle, leading to increased muscle weight and muscle fiber size. This target-selective photoinactivation strategy may expand the applicability of photoresponsive approaches for the treatment of various diseases, including muscular dystrophy.
items.authors: Kaoru Ikekawa, Hideyuki Okamoto, Shuko Amber Murano, Jo Yamamoto, Kota Inada, Sho Konno

items.title: A Systematic Approach to Batch Active Learning for Material Optimization
items.abstract: Closed-loop automated experimentation platforms are accelerating materials characterization and discovery, but their efficiency hinges on a question that automation alone does not answer: given a fixed evaluation budget, which experiment configurations should be run next? Batch active learning addresses this by selecting a group of candidates at each iteration, yet the design choices that govern its efficiency, how many candidates to acquire per cycle, and how to balance exploitation against exploration remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic in-silico benchmark of batch active learning across optimization landscapes, prediction models, and dimensionalities, introducing composite metrics that track optimization progress and surrogate accuracy as co-equal outcomes. We find that an exploitative-dominant strategy with a small fixed exploratory minority matches or exceeds purely exploitative configurations while outperforming purely exploratory ones across landscapes, models, and dimensionalities, and that batchand cycle-efficient regimes are distinct and constraint-dependent. We further validate these findings on an automated coacervate condensate optimization platform, confirming their transfer to a real, noisy materials system.
items.authors: Andrea Gardin, Willem van den Hout, Yannick H. A. Leurs, Luc Brunsveld, JanC. M. van Hest, Francesca Grisoni

items.title: Concerted, Facile CO2 Hydrogenation in Ni-MOF-74 Revealed by Machine Learning Interatomic Potential-Based Enhanced Sampling Simulations
items.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with open metal sites are promising heterogeneous catalysts, but the atomistic and dynamic details that govern their reactivity are difficult to access experimentally due to spatiotemporal resolution limits. Computational studies, predominantly gas-phase density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been used to study MOF-catalysed reactions, but typically rely on reduced cluster models of the metal center that neglect confinement effects or treat the framework as rigid during the reaction, limiting realistic modeling of catalysis at finite temperature and pressure. Here, we investigate, as a prototypical reaction, CO2 hydrogenation inside Ni-MOF-74 using machine learning interatomic potentials-based molecular dynamics and on-the-fly probability-based enhanced sampling (OPES) simulations, which delineate dynamic adsorption of CO2 and H2 in a flexible MOF and provide the underlying free energy for the CO2 reduction reaction. OPES simulations further reveal that H2 first adsorbs and undergoes heterolytic dissociation at the Ni-O site with a free energy barrier of ∼16 kcal mol−1, forming a proton and hydride species. Subsequent reduction of CO2 to HCOOH proceeds via a concerted mechanism, involving simultaneous hydride and proton transfer through a single transition state with a relatively low activation barrier of ∼6 kcal mol−1. These results demonstrate that explicit treatment of framework flexibility and thermodynamic conditions is essential to accurately capture reaction mechanisms and energetics in porous catalysts. Our integrated MLIP-OPES approach provides a generalizable computational framework for studying complex chemical transformations under confinement in MOFs and related framework materials.
items.authors: Dhananjay, Nishtha Sharma, Tarak Karmakar

items.title: Inter-Phase Chirality Transfer in 2D and Quasi-2D Perovskite Heterostructures
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) chiral metal halide perovskites (CMHPs) emerged as promising materials for spintronics. These 2D semiconductors comprise single layers of corner-sharing metal halide octahedra (n = 1) intercalated by organic cations, which limits charge mobility and spin lifetime. In comparison, quasi-2D analogs, with two or more octahedra layers (n ≥ 2), exhibit higher charge carriers mobility, augmented spin lifetime, and tailorable bandgap. Nonetheless, the few reports on quasi-2D CMHPs in the literature often describe time-consuming synthesis and materials presenting poor chiroptical properties after processing. We address this limitation by designing heterostructure thin films comprising a chiral n = 1 phase with a non-chiral n = 2 phase. Circular dichroism (CD) manifestation in the non-chiral phase confirms chirality transfer in the heterostructures. We found that chirality transfer depends on the intermolecular interaction of the chiral and non-chiral cations, being effective when R-/S-𝛼-methylbenzylammonium (MBA) in the chiral phase is combined with benzylammonium (BZA) in the non-chiral phase. Chirality transfer is weak when n-butylammonium (BA) is used in the non-chiral phase. We attribute this difference to a more effective intermixing enabled by 𝜋-𝜋 stacking in the MBA/BZA heterostructure. This inter-phase chirality transfer strategy opens a new avenue for spintronic materials design.
items.authors: Raphael F. Moral, Audrey R. Ryan, Jian Zhang, Paulo E. Marchezi, Ana F. Nogueira, Craig P. Schwartz

items.title: Order in Disorder: Exciton Dynamics Reveal Short-Range Molecular Packing in Small-Molecule Ionic Isolation Lattices Fluorescent Nanoparticles
items.abstract: Organic fluorescent nanoparticles (NPs) enable exceptional brightness through high dye loading, yet the fundamental relationship between local molecular organization and exciton dynamics remains elusive because short-range packing in densely packed assemblies is difficult to resolve using conventional structural characterization techniques. Here, femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals hidden short-range orientational order within globally disordered small-molecule ionic isolation lattice NPs (SMILES NPs) and establishes how this local organization governs exciton transport and fluorescence loss. Within locally ordered domains, fluorophore orientations are isotropically distributed within a two-dimensional plane perpendicular to the local stacking axis. Such local structural organization enables ultrafast exciton migration, followed by efficient energy funneling into non-emissive traps on a ~100 ps timescale, defining a kinetic window for exciton harvesting. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we introduce an emissive acceptor that captures excitons through sub-50 ps energy transfer, outcompeting trap-assisted quenching and producing binary SMILES NPs with a brightness per volume of 8700 M -1 cm -1 nm -3 , among the highest reported in the deep-red/near-infrared region. Collectively, this work establishes exciton dynamics as powerful probe of short-range molecular organization in dense molecular nanostructures and provides a molecular-packing-driven framework for controlling exciton transport and energy flow, offering general design principles for next-generation ultrabright emitters.
items.authors: Simin Jiang, Siyu Liu, Jakub Dostál, Amar H. Flood, Bo W. Laursen, Junsheng Chen

items.title: Breath Acetone Sensor for Subclinical Ketosis Detection in Dairy Cows
items.abstract: Subclinical ketosis (SCK) in dairy cows is a prevalent metabolic disorder that can reduce milk production, impair animal health, and causes substantial economic losses. Current diagnostic approaches are invasive and poorly suited for routine and autonomous on-farm detection. Here, we demonstrate non-invasive breath acetone sensing for monitoring metabolic changes associated with SCK in dairy cows. Breath samples (n = 235) were longitudinally collected over 35 days from seven dairy cows (five SCK-induced and two controls) using a custom-designed sampling mask. A chemoresistive sensor based on WO3 nanoparticles exhibited high selectivity toward acetone over interferents (e.g., ethanol, acetic acid, methane and isoprene) at their typical concentrations in cow breath and barn air. Good agreement (R2 = 0.81) with proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry was obtained for acetone quantification over a concentration range of 54 – 4,500 ppb. Time-resolved measurements revealed that the sensor captured dynamic post-partum acetone changes, including rapid increases, late-onset elevations, and stable low-level profiles. These trends were consistent with blood β-hydroxybutyrate and milk acetone measurements, supporting the physiological relevance of breath acetone as a non-invasive biomarker of SCK. These results demonstrate the potential of chemoresistive breath acetone sensing as a practical approach for longitudinal, on-farm monitoring of dairy cows for SCK detection.
items.authors: Jaehyun Ko, Jonas Hendricks, Anna-Maria Reiche, Frigga Dohme-Meier, Andreas T. Güntner

items.title: In Situ Co-Activation–Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution (ISCA–SNAR): Synthesis of a-Aryl-a-Heteroarylmalononitriles.
items.abstract: We report the discovery of a fundamentally unique nucleophilic aromatic substitution (S N Ar) reaction. It was found that a-arylmalononitriles and haloheterocycles undergo a mild, additive- and base-free C–C bond forming reaction via in situ co-activation (ISCA) to a carbanion and a pyridinium, which rapidly react through a neutral and low-barrier Meisenheimer complex to ultimately yield the S N Ar product. This study includes a background analysis of ISCA-S N Ar and a-aryl-a-heteroarylmalononitriles, discovery and optimization of efficient coupling conditions, a study of various physical organic parameters governing the transformation, scope of the reaction, and select malononitrile functional group interconversions. These detailed studies lay the groundwork for developing this, and related reactions, for use in high-value organic synthesis.
items.authors: Avneesh Kumar, Akash Gogate, Alexander Grenning

items.title: Reversible solidification of liquid organic hydrogen carriers
items.abstract: Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) are a promising option for hydrogen storage, but their transportation and long-term storage are complicated by sloshing, leakage, evaporation, and the associated safety issues. They are hard to gelate or solidify using conventional gelators due to factors such as steric hinderance and/or the lack of pi-pi conjugation within their molecular structure. Here, we report a one-pot reversible solidification strategy that converts hydrogenated LOHCs into free-standing monolithic solids without compromising their hydrogen-storage performance. The solidified carriers can prevent sloshing during transportation and potential leakage upon tank fail. The vapor pressure and fire intensity of LOHCs are reduced by 66% and 16.5%, respectively. As a result, their mass retention rate increased by 2.8-fold after one week of open storage and their mass loss rate is reduced by 3.4-fold after 24 hours of vigorous vibration compared with regular LOHCs.
items.authors: Xiaoying Lu, Yushuai Huang, Peng Peng, Libin Tian, Xiaokang Chen, Ziqing Mao

items.title: A Hidden Acid–Base Ion Pair Scaffolds Organic-Rich Atmospheric Nucleation
items.abstract: New particle formation is widely observed in organic-rich atmospheric environments where sulfuric acid and basic vapors appear scarce, yet what initiates nucleation and what role trace inorganic acid–base species play remain unclear. Guided by laboratory experiments and field observations, we resolve this ambiguity with a bottom-up framework bridging molecular energetics and nucleation kinetics, tracking nucleation from molecular origin to measurable formation rates. We uncover a hidden pathway in which a multifunctional oxygenated organic molecule (OOM) hydrogen-bonds simultaneously to sulfuric acid and ammonia, inducing proton transfer and stabilizing a charge-separated HSO 4 - –NH 4 + ion pair. This ion pair forms a localized electrostatic scaffold that recruits additional OOMs into a charge-assisted hydrogen-bond network, yielding stable embryonic clusters. Remarkably, a single ion pair unlocks this mechanism, indicating that even trace inorganic species can be indispensable nucleation triggers. Operating across diverse biogenic and anthropogenic OOM systems, ion-pair-scaffolded nucleation may be ubiquitous in the atmosphere.
items.authors: Huan Yang, Markku Kulmala, Renyi Zhang, Yafang Cheng

items.title: Coordinate bonding, cluster delocalization and topological criticality in a cyclic trimeric beryllium–dinitrogen complex
items.abstract: Fixation and coordination of molecular dinitrogen (N2) by main-group clusters offer fundamental insight into non-classical multi-centre bonding and light-metal activation pathways. Here we report a combined density-functional and ab initio study of the cyclic cluster Be3(N2)3. Geometry optimization and frequency analysis establish a stable, closed-shell Cs-symmetric trimer containing an isosceles triangular Be3 metal core coordinated end-on by three terminal N2 ligands. Energy decomposition analysis coupled with natural orbitals for chemical valence (ETS-NOCV) shows that the Be3⋯(N2)3 interaction is dominated by orbital contributions (≈60 % of attractive forces), supplemented by electrostatic attraction that together overcome Pauli repulsion. Quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) identifies two non-nuclear attractors along the apical–basal Be–Be edges, while electron localization function (ELF) and localized orbital locator (LOL) basin analyses reveal a distinct heart-shaped trisynaptic valence basin V(Be,Be,Be) populated by ≈1.8–2.0 electrons. These topological signatures establish multi-centre σ-aromatic delocalization as the structural foundation of the central metallacycle and demonstrate that light alkaline-earth elements can support non-classical N2 coordination frameworks.
items.authors: D K Jha, M Pathak, Dhananjay Kumar Jha

items.title: From Computational Chemistry to Generative Models: A Survey of AI-Driven Small-Molecule Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery requires navigating enormous chemical space to identify candidates that are simultaneously potent, selective, synthetically accessible, and acceptable across pharmacokinetic and safety profiles; modern generative AI extends a long computational medicinal chemistry lineage that began with QSAR, pharmacophore modeling, and early structure-based de novo design. This survey focuses primarily on developments from 2017 to 2025, with the literature updated through 31 January 2026. Using a medicinal-chemistry lens, it first establishes the shared machinery of the field: molecular representations such as SMILES, SELFIES, graphs, fingerprints, three-dimensional coordinates, voxels, and latent vectors; commonly used datasets and benchmarks; and graph neural network encoders, including message-passing, directional, and equivariant architectures. We compare five principal generative mechanisms—autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, normalizing flows, and diffusion models—together with reinforcement learning as a major goal-directed optimization framework. Across these approaches, we show that current methods offer complementary rather than interchangeable trade-offs, and we highlight recurring challenges, including validity versus synthesizability, limited prospective experimental validation, mode collapse and diversity loss, stereochemical and physical realism in three-dimensional design, computational cost, data scarcity, and the emerging convergence toward scaffold-conditioned generation, hybrid architectures, developability-aware optimization, and molecular foundation models.
items.authors: Houman Kazemzadeh, Kiarash Mokhtari, Nazanin Mirzaei, Seyed Reza Tavakoli, Ali Reza Keivanimehr, Shayan Majidifar

items.title: Nanothermodynamic Generalization of the Young–Laplace and Young Equations for Sessile Droplets with Line Effects
items.abstract: Thermodynamic investigations of wetting phenomena require that we handle the nanoscale. By combining Hill’s small-system thermodynamics with a Gibbsian composite-system description, we formulate the equilibrium thermodynamics of a sessile nanodroplet. We consider a one-component liquid droplet resting on an ideal, flat, inert solid substrate and in contact with reservoirs that fix the temperature and chemical potential. Finite-size effects are retained in the liquid bulk phase, the liquid–vapor interface, and the three-phase contact line, while the solid–vapor and solid–liquid interfaces are assumed to follow regular thermodynamics and treated macroscopically. The distinction between integral and differential pressure, surface tension, and line tension is used to derive nanothermodynamic generalizations of the Young–Laplace and Young equations. The resulting equations account for the size-and shape dependence of the finite thermodynamic contributions and recover the classical equilibrium equations in the macroscopic limit.
items.authors: Vitor H. C. Cunha, Signe Kjelstrup, Dick Bedeaux, Vitor Heitor Cardoso Cunha

items.title: Interfacial Position Governs the Dual Functionality of Carbazole Layers in Cu2O Photocathodes
items.abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid photoelectrodes offer a promising strategy to improve charge separation in photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems, yet the influence of the spatial position of ultrathin organic interlayers remains poorly understood. Herein, we integrate electropolymerized carbazole-based conjugated porous polymers (CPPs) into Cu2O photocathodes by positioning the polymer either beneath or on top of the semiconductor. Both hybrid architectures exhibit en-hanced PEC performance compared with bare Cu2O, with the highest photocur-rent achieved when the polymer is deposited as an ultrathin overlayer. A combi-nation of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy together with femtosecond and nanosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the carbazole interlayer performs two distinct functions depending on its position within the hybrid architecture. When located beneath Cu2O, the polymer primarily facili-tates directional hole extraction and charge separation. In contrast, when depos-ited on top of Cu2O, the ultrathin polymer predominantly passivates surface defects, suppressing interfacial recombination and extending charge-carrier life-times while preserving efficient interfacial charge transfer. The triscarbazole-based polymer consistently exhibits slightly improved charge-transport proper-ties compared with its biscarbazole analogue. These findings demonstrate that the functionality of ultrathin organic interlayers is governed not only by their molecular structure but also by their spatial position within hybrid photoelec-trodes. More broadly, this work establishes interfacial positioning as a simple yet powerful design principle for engineering charge-carrier dynamics in organic-inorganic photoelectrochemical systemsgoes here.
items.authors: Alejandro García-Eguizábal, Miguel Garcí­a-Tecedor, Miguel Gomez-Mendoza, Freddy Oropeza, Soranyel Gonzalez-Carrero, James R. Durrant

items.title: Efficiency and Accessibility Are Not Enough: Chemical-Validity Filtering in High-Throughput Screening of Organic Photovoltaic Materials
items.abstract: Descriptor-based screening for organic photovoltaics ranks molecules on computed properties such as frontier-orbital energies and synthetic accessibility, but such descriptors do not test whether a highly ranked molecule is a chemically sensible material. We screened 17,458 molecules from the PubChemQC database using PCESAScore—Scharber-model efficiency minus the RDKit synthetic-accessibility score—and examined what the metric actually returns. Seven molecules cross the viability threshold, but three are not organic semiconductors (molecular oxygen, a magnesium carbonate salt, a quinhydrone cocrystal) and three more carry reactive groups (two azides, one nitroso). A transparent chemicalvalidity filter and a reactive-group screen reduce the viable set from seven to four to a single stable candidate. The top-ranked molecule, an azidotriazine, reaches a 36.1% nominal efficiency—above the Scharber model’s single-junction ceiling—from a 0.91 eV gap, and carries a 9.26 D dipole and a negative computed reorganization energy: signatures of an unusable material, not a lead. Across the dataset, heteroatom composition correlates only weakly with orbital energies (|r| ≤ 0.34), so no simple design rule holds. Descriptor-based materials screens require an explicit chemical-validity and stability gate; the gap between the pre-and post-gate viable sets is a result in itself.
items.authors: Patrick Sorrel Mvoto Kongo, Steve Cabrel Teguia Kouam, Jean-Pierre TCHAPET NJAFA, Serge Guy Nana Engo

items.title: Stannylene Ambiphilicity Enables Formation of a Trimetallic Complex
items.abstract: Low-valent heavier group 14 tetrylenes combine a stereochemically active lone pair with a vacant p-orbital at a single centre, resulting in a unique ambiphilic reactivity profile. However, exploiting these donor–acceptor properties to construct transition-metal complexes featuring bridging tetrylene units remains largely unexplored. Here we report a flexible pincer ligand in which an N,O,N pocket stabilises the monomeric stannylene [(PNONP)Sn] (Sn1) that itself presents a P,Sn,P pocket for nickel coordination and can be employed, either stepwise or in one pot, to afford the isolable NHC-stabilised tin–nickel heterobimetallics [(PNONP)SnNi(NHC)] Sn4a,b (NHC = N-heterocyclic carbene). Reaction of Sn4a with W(CO)6, envisaged as a simple test electrophile for the tin-centred lone pair, instead proceeds via unanticipated NHC-to-CO exchange and the resulting NHC-free tin–nickel-carbonyl fragment self-associates to give the dimeric complex [(PNONP)SnNi(CO)]2 (Sn5). Treatment of Sn4a with [(p-cymene)Ru(Cl)2]2 affords the target heterotrimetallic Ni–Sn–Ru complex [(PNONP)Sn{Ru(Cl)2(p-cyemene)}Ni(IiPr2Me2)] (Sn6), in which tin bridges the metal centres in a genuinely push–pull fashion, representing the first structurally authentification of such a bonding mode for a heavy tetrylene.
items.authors: Jonathan Kieselbach, Christopher Golz, Jasmin Alsadi, Josh Abbenseth, Malte Fischer

items.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of functionalized polymers on primary human T cells
items.abstract: Polymers can be designed to impart new functions to the surfaces of tissues and cells, making them valuable tools for bioengineering applications. Existing grafting-to methods suffer from low polymer grafting efficiencies – due in part to challenging-to-control lipid anchoring strategies. One solution to these limitations is to adopt a grafting-from approach, where polymers are synthesized at defined initiation sites on the cell surface. Previous studies have highlighted the value of cytocompatible photocatalyzed grafting-from polymer chemistries or site-specific covalent anchoring of initiation sites; however, unification of these features remains unexplored. Further, no grafting-from technologies have been applied to surface engineering of primary human cells. To address this gap, we have combined Photo-Induced Electron-Transfer Reversible Addition-Fragmentation Chain-Transfer (PET-RAFT) chemistry with site selective surface anchoring of a custom traceable oligomeric polymer initiation site. We show that our approach enabled efficient grafting-from chain extension of functionally diverse polymers anchored on cell surface carbohydrates (glycans). The approach was compatible with both an immortalized human cell line and primary human immune cells (T cells). This technology provides a framework for site-selective modification of primary cell surfaces without genetic manipulation.
items.authors: Olivia Mann-Delany, Fauzia N. Izzati, Richard Fuku, Jon Babi, Qingyu Shi, Vanessa Affe

items.title: Extended QM/Me: Quantum-Mechanical Explicit Solvation at Solid–Liquid Interfaces
items.abstract: We extend the subtractive QM/Me embedding scheme from vacuum to liquid environments: the adsorbate and explicit solvent are treated by a periodic quantum-mechanical layer above a classical metal bath, avoiding the need for metal–solvent interaction parameters. For methoxy on Pt(111) in water (3070 quantum atoms), the performance of three tight-binding Hamiltonians for adiabatic solvation shifts is assessed. The embedding provides analytic energy gradients and substantially reduced computational cost compared to a fully quantum-mechanical model.
items.authors: You Lu, Thomas W. Keal

items.title: Toward Property-Directed Catalytic Skeletal Editing of Functional Organic Materials
items.abstract: Late-stage skeletal editing has emerged as a useful strategy in synthetic and medicinal chemistry for altering molecular frameworks by atom insertion, deletion, replacement, or bond reorganization. Functional organic molecules and materials are commonly optimized through peripheral substitution and de novo framework construction. Direct modification of an existing skeleton provides a complementary means of tuning electronic structure, molecular shape, chirality, packing, and processability. Herein we examine catalytic skeletal editing with an emphasis on functional organic materials, specifically π-conjugated molecules, dyes, polymers, and covalent frameworks. Representative examples are evaluated in terms of catalytic status and experimentally demonstrated properties. Key requirements for broader application include site selectivity, element transfer, catalyst compatibility, and control of editing extent in extended materials. The emerging opportunity is to move skeletal editing from reaction-centered diversification toward catalyst-controlled, property-directed modification.
items.authors: Taichi Koike, Sajan Pradhan, Kenichiro Itami

items.title: Single-particle FRET reveals ligand configurations on colloidal perovskite quantum dots
items.abstract: The functionality of colloidal quantum dots (QDs), whether in fundamental studies, optoelectronics, or emerging quantum technologies, critically depends on their surface chemistry, with organic ligands influencing nearly every aspect of their behavior. Whereas the inorganic core can be comprehensively characterized at atomic resolution, ligands remain dibicult to probe owing to their low atomic contrast and soft, disordered structure. Here, we empower single-particle photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy to resolve ligand conformations at sub-nanometer resolution. Tagging ligand tails with organic dyes enables measuring their distance from the QD via Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Single-particle, single-molecule FRET experiments performed on lead halide perovskite QDs reveal nanometer-scale variations in dye-surface distances, both within individual particles (0.81 ± 0.22 nm on average) and between QDs with varied ligand chemistries (from 0.25 nm to 1.02 nm). Supported by atomistic modelling, our experiments tie variations in the local ligand environment to this conformational diversity. A powerful yet accessible spectroscopic method for interrogating the complex surface chemistry of QDs is highly relevant to QD-based optoelectronics, quantum applications, and photocatalysis.
items.authors: Leon G. Feld, Oleksandr Kolomiiets, Noah Shahin, Sebastian Sabisch, Gabriele Rainò, Maksym V. Kovalenko

items.title: Vicinal Chlorination of Dehydrogenated Polyethylene Toward Applications of Waste Polyolefins
items.abstract: Post-polymerization vicinal chlorination of unsaturated polyolefins provides access to linear poly(ethylene-co-1,2-dichloroethylene) polymers that are inaccessible through conventional polymerization or post-polymerization routes. Herein, Cl 2 (g), generated in situ from N-chlorosuccinimide (NCS) and hydrochloric acid (HCl), was used to selectively convert alkene sites in polycyclooctene (PCOE)-derived polyolefins into vicinal chloride subunits. Partial hydrogenation of PCOE afforded substrates containing 4–25 mol% residual C=C, which upon chlorination, yielded polymers with controlled levels and distributions of vicinal chlorides along a linear polyethylene backbone. Incorporation of chlorides into the PCOE-derived polymers disrupts crystal formation and reduces the glass transition and melting temperatures. For the 25 mol% vicinal chloride, the polymer affords precise placement of chlorides along the polymer backbone and transforms the orthorhombic crystal structure, typical of polyethylene (PE), to a triclinic crystal structure, suggesting the incorporation of Cl atoms to the crystallites. This method was further extended to dehydrogenated post-consumer HDPE from milk jugs, affording vicinal chlorinated polyethylene containing ~ 1.1 mol% vicinal Cl, while maintaining the original polymer chain architecture and molecular weight. These results establish vicinal chlorination of unsaturated PE as a strategy for tuning polymer properties and provide a platform for upcycling PEs into value-added functional materials.
items.authors: Pedro M. Jimenez Antenucci, Tingfeng Chen, Hoda Shokrollahzadeh Behbahani, Huapei Qiu, Lucia Lavelle, Emily Sidlow

items.title: Cooperative Inorganic-Organic Binding Sites in Zeolite Adsorbents Enhance CO 2 Capture and Water Resistance
items.abstract: Optimization of amine-based adsorbents for carbon capture technologies requires next-generation materials capable of handling a broad range of operating conditions with high amine efficiency. The current disadvantages of liquid amine absorbents motivate the design of porous solid analogues as alternatives. Here we present a bifunctional zeolite comprised of silanol defects and grafted amines that cooperatively bind CO 2 with 97% amine efficiency. We use a borosilicate beta zeolite as a parent material and generate a high density of silanol defects through facile post-synthesis demetalation, followed by amine functionalization. Spectroscopic techniques and density functional theory calculations confirm that silylpropylcarbamate species enhance CO 2 binding through an activated process with optimal performance at 100℃, which markedly reduces the temperature swing for regeneration without loss in performance after multiple cycles. Systematic analysis of carbon capture performance reveals that CO 2 sorption capacity doubles when shifting from high to low temperature, and is positively influenced by humidity.
items.authors: Debasmita Halder, Mingze Zheng, Hardik K. Balsaraf, Taimin Yang, Zachariah J. Berkson, Brandon C. Bukowski

items.title: Benzimidazole Modification of DNA Aptamers for Ultra Responsive Protein-Induced Fluorescence Enhancement
items.abstract: Post-SELEX incorporation of environmentally responsive fluorescent nucleobase surrogates provides a powerful strategy for converting DNA aptamers into protein aptasensors, yet achieving large protein-induced fluorescence enhancement (PIFE) while preserving target affinity remains a major challenge.Here, we introduce a photobasic 4-(1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)-N,N-dimethylaniline (AnIm) nucleobase surrogate that enables ultraresponsive PIFE through site-specific incorporation into DNA aptamers.As a model system, AnIm was incorporated into two thrombin-binding aptamers that recognize distinct protein exosites: the 15-mer TBA15 and the 27-mer HD22.The modified aptamers retained high thrombin affinity (Kd = 85-167 nM).Within HD22, site-dependent fluorescence enhancements of 70-108-fold (Irel) were observed, affording a limit of detection (LOD) of 280 pM in PBS and 3.8 nM in 5% human serum.To our knowledge, this >100-fold fluorescence turn-on represents the largest PIFE response reported for a fluorescent nucleobase surrogate.Spectroscopic studies reveal that the exceptional sensitivity arises from a protein-induced pKa shift coupled with suppression of a twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) state.Protein binding shifts AnIm from its protonated (NH⁺) ground-state toward the neutral (N) form, reducing background fluorescence, while excited-state protonation generates a fluorescent molecular rotor whose emission is enhanced within the rigid protein microenvironment.These findings establish photobasic nucleobase surrogates as a general strategy for post-SELEX fluorescent aptamer engineering for ultra-responsive PIFE-based biosensing.
items.authors: Matteo Pavlovic, Austin Pounder, Naomi Varnovitski, Stacey D. Wetmore, Richard A. Manderville

items.title: Spacing Over Sequence: Design Considerations for Polystyrene-binding Polypeptides
items.abstract: Plastic-binding polypeptides have emerging applications in biosensor design, materials functionalization, and nanoplastic capture, and the rational design of new sequences requires the development of structural and sequence-based design principles. Here, we demonstrate a computational workflow combining atomistic molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling to evaluate polypeptide binding to polystyrene, a common commodity plastic. We investigate two candidate sequences previously proposed as polystyrene binders, both enriched in either aromatic or cationic residues expected to interact with polystyrene's aromatic rings. We find that the two sequences bind stably through apparent π-stacking and cation-π interactions. These binding modalities rely on proper residue spacing; not all cationic residues on a polypeptide bind unless separated by linking residues as demonstrated by our “arginine claw” motif. We also determine that the presence of the polypeptide does shield the polystyrene from contacts with solvent, though it does not promote further self-collapse of the oligomer. Our analysis demonstrates how sequence composition coupled with sequence orientation enables multiple binding modalities, determining motifs such as the “arginine claw” and aromatic ring distribution that can be leveraged in future polypeptide design.
items.authors: Mansi Gokani, Brianna Z. Fea, Ashley Z. Guo

items.title: Which state are you converging? A spin audit of sample-based quantum diagonalization benchmarks on iron–sulfur clusters
items.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD/QSCI) diagonalizes the Hamiltonian classically in determinant subspaces selected from quantum-circuit samples. Its iron–sulfur demonstrations underpin claims of utility-scale quantum chemistry, and a recent critique disputes them at matched subspace dimension. Both sides compare energies; neither reports which spin state was computed. Our spin audit uses the exact determinant-space ⟨S²⟩, the invariant spectrum of the S² block over quasi-degenerate manifolds, and higher moments (⟨S⁴⟩ to ⟨S⁸⟩) bounding the spin-sector weights. We apply it to the public [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] benchmarks, IBM's released qiskit-addon-sqd pipeline and published hardware data. No audited execution returned the named singlet at competitive energy; for published states unavailable to direct audit, the energy-only records do not establish singlet identity. Under the audited HCI protocols, selected-CI growth approaches a spin-contaminated state (⟨S²⟩ ≈ 4.7 on [2Fe-2S]) whose samples keep the contamination. Spin-inversion completion leaves the energy and ⟨S²⟩ of these states unchanged. The released [2Fe-2S] hardware samples give no energy advantage over the released uniform-random control. A scalar mean does not identify these states: two audited arms share ⟨S²⟩ ≈ 2.00, but one is a triplet eigenstate (Var(S²) = 3×10⁻⁶) and the other a 2:1 singlet–quintet mixture whose third moment bounds its triplet weight below 10⁻⁴. At the largest published dimension (5.625×10⁷ determinants, reconstructed here from the released support), the lowest root, 170 mHa below the published energy, has ⟨S²⟩ = 1.3711, unchanged under an 18.6-fold residual tightening to 1.1% of the 0.285 mHa gap. Its first two moments, with Var(S²) = 6.9, exclude any decomposition confined to S ≤ 2. Near-singlet character appears only as a non-stationary superposition, because determinant selection does not commute with S². Energy-only benchmarks therefore do not establish convergence to the named state. We recommend reporting spin moments with every energy and controlling spin during selection.
items.authors: Tyler Vitale

items.title: Nitrile Geometry as an Architectural Code for Cu10 Nanocluster Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Atomically precise nanoclusters offer molecularly defined metal architectures, yet their conversion into extended frameworks remains difficult because reticulation must impose long-range order without erasing the structural adaptability of the multinuclear node. Here, we show that nitrile geometry can function as an architectural code for Cu10 nanocluster metal–organic frameworks (NCMOFs). Rather than relying on conventional pyridyl donors, we employ sterically minimal aryl nitriles whose weaker donor character is coupled to sharply defined coordination vectors. Natural population analysis confirms that nitrile N atoms are substantially less electron-rich than representative pyridyl donors, establishing a distinct electronic regime for cluster reticulation. Using terephthalonitrile (TPN), isophthalonitrile (IPN), and 1,3,5-tricyanobenzene (TCB), we obtain four crystallographically distinct frameworks— Cu10TPN-1D, Cu10IPN-2D, Cu10IPN-1D, and Cu10TCB-2Dthrough diffusion-controlled assembly of a common Cu–thiolate precursor. Single-crystal structures reveal that the Cu–N interface remains comparatively constrained, while Cu···Cu, Cu–S, and especially Cu–O metrics reorganize to accommodate different linker vectors and lattice demands. Strikingly, the same 120° IPN linker yields either 1D or 2D connectivity depending on the crystallization medium, demonstrating that linker geometry defines an accessible connectivity landscape rather than a predetermined topology. These results establish a broader design principle for NCMOFs: directional information can be encoded in a weakly donating linker, while structural compliance is retained within the nanocluster node, enabling adaptive multinuclear units to translate molecular geometry into distinct reticular states.
items.authors: Ayumu Kondo, Riki Nakatani, Sreelakshmi K. S., Tsukasa Irie, Yunosuke Arai, Yuya Sugawara

items.title: Integrated CO2 removal and NH3 recovery from wastewater using a bidirectionally productive electrochemical pH swing
items.abstract: Electrochemical pH-swing processes based on proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) offer a promising route for selective chemical separation from aqueous media. Yet in all previous systems only one half of the pH swing performs a separation, while the reverse half is expended solely to regenerate the state of charge of the active electrode or electrolyte. Using a synthetic mimic of domestic wastewater as the input feed, we demonstrate a bidirectionally productive electrochemical pH-swing generated by a phenazine-carbon nanotube PCET-active composite electrode in an aqueous flow cell, in which both the acidifying and alkalizing half-cycles perform useful chemical separation. Electrode oxidation acidifies the wastewater to convert dissolved inorganic carbon into CO 2 (aq) for removal, whereas the subsequent reduction alkalizes the feed, converting NH 4 + to NH 3 (aq) for recovery using membrane stripping. An experimentally validated reaction-transport model establishes the pH-swing sequence as a key design parameter, with oxidation before reduction enabling integrated CO 2 removal and NH 3 recovery, whereas the opposite sequence prioritizes NH 3 recovery through near-complete NH 4 + -to-NH 3 conversion. The system achieved batchwise NH 3 recovery using the reduction–oxidation sequence over 31 cycles spanning 43 h, establishing operational stability over a duration not previously demonstrated for PCET-driven nutrient recovery. The oxidation–reduction sequence achieved average energetic costs of 219.9 kJ mol -1 CO 2 removed and 12.2 kWh kg -1 N recovered, with corresponding separation rates of 4.47 μmol CO 2 h -1 cm -2 and 5.33 g N m -2 day -1 , respectively. By making both directions of an electrochemical pH swing productive, this work reframes electrode regeneration as an opportunity for a second separation, and points toward wastewater treatment plants as distributed sites for combined nutrient recovery and carbon removal.
items.authors: Bin Yun, Orçun Dinçer, Marc-Antoni Goulet, David G. Kwabi

items.title: Machine-Learning Models Bypass Charge Computation for Modeling 14N Quadrupolar Relaxation in Ionic Liquids
items.abstract: Modeling the electric field gradient (EFG) in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enables the prediction of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) relaxation rates thus allowing to unravel the underlying relaxation-active molecular motion. Here, we compare the linear-response Sternheimer model with a novel machine-learning (ML) approach to simulate 14 N quadrupolar T 1 relaxation in the ionic liquid 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([BMIM][BF 4 ]). Improving the parametrization of the Sternheimer model at the low-symmetry nitrogen sites required an electron density-based charge-partitioning scheme. In contrast, the parameter-free ML descriptor directly captured the EFG dynamics, providing a flexible methodology for computing EFG tensors in complex ionic systems. In the extreme-narrowing regime, both models predicted relaxation rates in excellent agreement with experimental measurements. Finally, using a regularized inverse Laplace transform, we deconvolute the dynamics of the EFG tensor and of the cation inertia tensor, and identify molecular rotation as the dominant mode responsible for 14 N quadrupolar relaxation.
items.authors: Federico Civaia, Yanan Li, Florin Teleanu, Simone S. Köcher, Josef Granwehr, Alexej Jerschow

items.title: An Atomistic Workflow for Determining Acid-Base Prototropic Tautomer Microstate Populations
items.abstract: We present a new cheminformatics package, Protomer Enumerator Automatic Calculator for Energies (PEACE), which lists the prototropic forms of a given acid or base, and predicts which of these microstates are likely to be present in solution. The workflow enumerates prototropic tautomers, and orchestrates inexpensive semi-empirical quantum chemical simulations to evaluate their single-point energies, solvation free energies, entropic contributions, and ultimately their solution-phase energies. The relative population of each tautomer is then calculated. PEACE includes automatic error checks, tautomer screening, and conformational effects to improve speed and accuracy. It can be run in several solvent systems and on charged solutes. Herein, we demonstrate the workflow’s efficacy on numerous practical benchmarks including on druglike molecules. The workflow is freely available for use through the command line with minimal package dependencies.
items.authors: Jonathan Wenyuan Zheng, Esther Heid

items.title: Small Organic Molecules Regulate Transport-Limited Dendrite Growth in Aqueous Zn Battery Anodes
items.abstract: Understanding electrochemical crystal growth at high rates and under far-fromequilibrium conditions is important for a broad range of industrial processes, including metal electrowinning, semiconductor plating, and electrochemical energy storage. In particular, transport-limited metal electrodeposition, which often produces aggressive dendritic morphologies, plays a critical role in the behavior of fast-charging battery anodes. Although small organic molecules such as urea are known to influence electrodeposition, their effects have primarily been studied at moderate current densities well below the mass-transport limit. Here, we investigate how urea affects Zn metal growth in concentrated aqueous battery electrolytes (10 M ZnCl2) under explicitly transport-limited conditions. Using operando visualization together with ex situ characterization, we find that urea transforms Zn dendrite structure once its concentration exceeds a threshold. In the absence of organic additives, Zn forms quasi-single-crystalline, needlelike dendrites whose crystallites exhibit apparent orientational correlation across the entire dendrite, over length scales of centimeters. This behavior suggests sustained growth from a small number of initially nucleated crystals. In contrast, above 5 wt.% urea, the dendrites initially lose their long-range orientational correlation before reverting to needle-like propagation. We attribute this transition to urea adsorption on the Zn surface, which modifies the relative kinetics of nucleation and crystal growth. Comparisons with structurally related small molecules indicate that molecular symmetry and functional group selection play an important role in governing this behavior: asymmetrical acetamide yields needle-like growth similar to the additive-free baseline, whereas retaining symmetry with methyl groups using acetone provides a dense morphology that extends cell lifespan. These findings provide new insight into the molecular regulation of electrochemical crystal growth under far-from-equilibrium conditions and may inform strategies for controlling Zn deposition in fast-charging aqueous batteries.
items.authors: Alex Kretzschmar, Kent J. X. Zheng

items.title: High-Entropy Catalysts for Lithium-Sulfur and Room-Temperature Sodium-Sulfur Batteries: Electronic Descriptors, Performance, and Design Challenges
items.abstract: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) and room-temperature sodium-sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries offer high theoretical energy density at low materials cost, but the insulating nature of sulfur, the shuttling of soluble polysulfides, and sluggish multistep redox kinetics limit their practical use. Catalysts that anchor polysulfides and accelerate their conversion are a widely investigated remedy, and the field is moving from single-metal catalysts toward high-entropy catalysts (HECs) built from five or more principal elements. This review is organized around the electronic descriptors, principally the d-band center and its refinements, that are used to connect multi-element composition to polysulfide adsorption and to reaction barriers. We define configurational entropy quantitatively, separate genuine HECs from lower-order multimetal catalysts, survey the alloy, oxide, sulfide, and single-atom families with attention to mechanism and limitations, and treat the still under-demonstrated RT Na-S case explicitly. We then examine the first-principles workflow required for chemically disordered surfaces and the emerging, mostly non-sulfur, use of machine learning (ML). Our central conclusion is that the d-band center is a useful but non-universal descriptor whose predictive value depends on local coordination, oxidation state, surface reconstruction, solvation, and polysulfide coverage, and that direct evidence for entropy-derived synergy, and for high-entropy catalysis in RT Na-S specifically, remains incomplete.
items.authors: Nusrat Jahan Hridita, Md. Safin Mahmood Shomyo

items.title: Hydrogen diffusion on metals: Full-Dimensional Ring Polymer Molecular Dynamics Rate Calculations
items.abstract: The diffusion of hydrogen atoms on nine different metals: Co, Ni, Cu, Rh, Pd, Ag, Ir, Pt, Au, has been simulated by ring polymer molecular dynamics. For Co, the (0001) surface facet has been chosen, while for all other metals, (100) surfaces are investigated. For the nine systems, message-passing atomic cluster expansion (MACE) machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) were set up by means of self-consistent biased fine-tunings. The H diffusion was sampled first with the MACE MP-0 foundation model by means of umbrella samplings along the diffusion path; then, a subset of sampled structures was recalculated by periodic density-functional theory (DFT) and the MACE was fine-tuned with the obtained reference data. This was repeated once to correct for biases of the foundation model concerning the sampling of configuration space. Thorough benchmarking revealed that the fine-tuned MLIPs were reliable and of high quality, also for situations not covered by the training set. The fine-tuned MACE MLIPs were then used to sample the full-dimensional diffusion rate constants with the Caracal program for temperatures between 20 and 300 K, in 10 K steps, and from them obtain the temperature-dependent diffusion coefficients. Crossover temperatures to the deep tunneling regime were calculated as well.
items.authors: Julien Steffen

items.title: Case Study of Bayesian Batch Optimization Strategies for Heterogeneous Catalysts in CO2 Hydrogenation
items.abstract: High-throughput and automated experimentation platforms combined with artificial intelligence are increasingly used to accelerate catalyst discovery. Batch Bayesian optimization (BO) (i.e., the simulta neous selection of multiple candidate experiments per iteration) is widely adopted for navigating large compositional spaces; however, its practical behavior under realistic high-throughput and batch con straints remains poorly understood. In this work, we performed a case study on four BO strategies to optimize the catalyst composition for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. For each BO strategy, 48 catalysts were synthesized by co-precipitation, utilizing an automated synthesis platform, and evaluated in high-throughput fixed-bed reactors over seven batch iterations. The composition space comprised up to four metallic elements selected from a pool of nine. Although all BO strategies identified competitive catalyst formulations, most optimization trajectories rapidly converged toward distinct local optima that were strongly influenced by the initial random design and exhibited limited global exploration of the compositional space. This case study provides practical insights into the limitations of BO for batch catalyst optimization and highlights their strong dependence on the initial random design, parameter space definition, and batch execution strategy.
items.authors: Erwin Lam, Kourosh Shariat, Leo Chevalier, Guillaume Draznieks, Scott Sussex, Riccardo De Santi

items.title: Cross-Conjugation Effect in Benzotrithiophene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Bandgap engineering in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is critical for their optoelectronic and photocatalytic applications, but it remains far less developed compared to linear p-conjugated polymers. Here, we demonstrate that permutation of π-conjugation pathway provides a general strategy to tune the electronic structure of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). An asymmetric benzotrithiophene ( A BTT) node enables a more efficient electron delocalization compared to its commonly used symmetric analogue ( S BTT), resulting in ∼0.05–0.2 eV band-gap contraction and improved charge-transport properties in corresponding COFs, with electrical conductivity up to 1.6×10 –1 S cm –1 in iodine-doped films.
items.authors: Mohammad Hossein Gohari, Chang Wan Kang, Pegah Ghamari, Cory Ruchlin, Ting Yu, Dmytro F. Perepichka

items.title: Backbone Editing of Natural Rubber for Sustainable Flexible Electronics
items.abstract: Sustainable electronics offer a path to reducing the environmental burden of electronic waste, but achieving closed-loop recyclability in flexible organic devices remains challenging because most stretchable substrates and elastomers are non-recyclable, petroleum-derived thermosets. Natural rubber ( cis -1,4-polyisoprene), a renewable and mechanically compliant biopolymer, is an attractive alternative for sustainable electronics, yet its chemical inertness has limited its use in advanced functional materials. Here we report a photoredox-catalyzed strategy for the selective functionalization of cis -1,4-polyisoprene, enabling modular installation of functional groups without crosslinking or degradation. This approach yields functional polyisoprene with luminescent and flame-retardant properties and, through dynamic ionic crosslinking, produces elastomers with tensile strengths up to 20 MPa and stretch ratios of 22. We further prepare a recyclable composite using functional natural rubber and PEDOT:PSS, stabilized by ionic interactions rather than permanent vulcanized networks, that retains mechanical and electrical performance over multiple recycling cycles. Its application in robotic motion sensing and electronic skin exemplifies a fundamental design principle for sustainable flexible electronics.
items.authors: Zongnan Zhang, Linkun Liu, Luke Chang, Mengmeng Liu, Lin Cheng, Hua Zhong

items.title: Machine-learning force-field scoring rivals free-energy perturbation for congeneric ligand ranking across public benchmarks
items.abstract: Relative binding free-energy (RBFE) methods such as free-energy perturbation (FEP) set the accuracy standard for ranking congeneric ligands in structurebased drug design, but their computational cost limits throughput. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) now approach quantum-chemical accuracy at a small fraction of that cost, raising the question of whether they can recover much of RBFE’s ranking accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. We introduce a static-score methodology called taqo and benchmark 10 MLFF variants spanning 6 model families (UMA, MACE, Orb, eSEN, AIMNet2, AllScAIP), together with a classical molecular-mechanics force field, on a uniform staticpocket protocol, correlated against experiment across 22 benchmark systems.We find that the ten MLFFs cannot be resolved from one another at this sample size, while every one of them significantly outranks the classical force field reference, at a few seconds per ligand on a single GPU. Against published OpenFE and FEP+ results on the same systems and the same ligand sets, taqo is statistically indistinguishable from OpenFE and significantly below FEP+, at roughly three orders of magnitude lower cost. On the congeneric JACS subset taqo and FEP+ are statistically indistinguishable. On the same benchmark poses taqo outperforms classical docking scores and is statistically indistinguishable from deep-learning affinity models, without any affinity-specific training. Together these establish MLFF interaction-energy scoring as a practical high-throughput approach for lead optimization.
items.authors: Kevin Ryczko, Sarah Maier, Amogh Sood, Patrick Rowe, Harish Ramadas, Lorenzo Boninsegna

items.title: Direct Synthesis of Covalent Organic Framework Monolayer via Ullmann Coupling on Non-metallic Substrates
items.abstract: Two-dimensional covalent organic framework monolayers are promising porous materials for electronic and optoelectronic applications owing to their periodic nanoporous architectures and tunable electronic structures. However, on-surface Ullmann coupling used to construct such frameworks typically relies on catalytic single-crystal metal substrates, whose strong electronic coupling can obscure the intrinsic properties of the molecular layer and complicate device integration. Here, we demonstrate substrate-engineered Ullmann coupling of 1,3,5-tris(4iodophenyl)benzene toward monolayer two-dimensional covalent organic networks on nonmetallic substrates. On inert highly oriented pyrolytic graphite, externally deposited Fe species promote C–I bond activation and covalent coupling, whereas FeO thin films enable network formation without additional metal deposition through defect-derived Fe active centers. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the energetically favored pathways on HOPG, FeO, and Au(111) all involve transient metal-centered intermediates that facilitate dehalogenation and C–C bond formation, although the catalytic centers originate from different sources. Bias-dependent scanning tunneling microscopy further shows that substrate coupling governs the visibility of frontier electronic states: weakly interacting HOPG preserves orbital-like features that closely resemble calculated frontier states of the freestanding framework, whereas stronger interactions on FeO and Au(111) progressively perturb or screen these states. These results establish nonmetallic substrates as viable platforms for on-surface Ullmann coupling and highlight substrate engineering as a strategy for accessing intrinsic electronic properties of two-dimensional covalent organic materials.
items.authors: Dong Nie, Jingyu He, Jinwei Fan, Siming Gu, Junqi He, Hafiza Saima Batoola

items.title: Finite-Field Second Hyperpolarizability via Adaptive Bayesian Quantum Phase Estimation for Early Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers: Ground-State Energies Beyond Chemical Accuracy
items.abstract: The static second hyperpolarizability governs third-order nonlinear-optical responses but is difficult to compute by first-principles methods because finite-field extraction requires a fourth-order energy derivative. The resulting error amplification demands sub-µHa ground-state energies, far beyond conventional chemical accuracy. Standard multi-qubit QPE can in principle meet this precision but requires a wide ancilla register, while single-ancilla iterative QPE (IQPE) is limited by a binary-grid quantization floor. We develop an adaptive Bayesian QPE (BQPE) workflow that uses a single ancilla, terminal measurements, and real-time classical feedback to estimate the eigenphase through a continuous posterior rather than a fixed binary grid. For a linear H4 chain in the STO-3G basis, represented by a six-qubit parity Hamiltonian with one ancilla, BQPE reaches a ground-state energy error of ≈ 10−7 Ha at controlled-U depth mmax ≈ 215, about two orders of magnitude below the IQPE floor. Propagated through the finite-field stencil and Richardson extrapolation, these energies recover the second hyperpolarizability within ±10% of the FCI reference over the stable field-strength plateau, whereas IQPE at the same depth fails to do so. These results indicate that grid-free Bayesian phase estimation can make nonlinear-optical properties accessible on early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
items.authors: Katsuki Okuno

items.title: P,T-odd sensitivity parameters of laser-coolable SrOH from relativisticcoupled-cluster theory
items.abstract: Ultracold molecules have attracted significant interest as promising platforms for exploring fundamental physics and quantum information science. As progress toward precision measurements with the ultracold SrOH molecule is currently underway [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 083401 (2025)}], we present a four-component relativistic coupled-cluster (RCC) study of various parity- and time-reversal-violating (P,T-odd) interactions in the ground electronic state of SrOH. In particular, we extend the application of the Z-vector (energy-derivative) approach within the RCC framework to a polyatomic molecule for the calculation of P,T-odd molecular sensitivity parameters. We obtain the following molecular parameters for SrOH: $E_\text{eff} = 2.12 \pm 0.27$~GV/cm, $W_S = 1.89 \pm 0.21$~kHz, and $W_M = (2.04 \pm 0.12) \times 10^{32}$~Hz/e$\cdot$cm$^2$. These parameters provide essential molecular inputs for the design and interpretation of precision experiments with SrOH. We find that the P,T-odd sensitivity parameters of SrOH are comparable to those of the isoelectronic diatomic molecule SrF. However, the polyatomic structure of SrOH offers enhanced capabilities for suppressing systematic errors, making it a particularly promising candidate for high-precision searches for P,T violation.
items.authors: Kaushik Talukdar, Himangshu Das, Sishmita Tamang, Malaya K Nayak

items.title: Increasing Trifluoroacetic Acid Concentration in Austrian Groundwater and Its Associations with Agricultural Indicators
items.abstract: Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) is an extremely persistent and highly mobile substance that is accumulating in the environment as a result of continued emissions from diverse sources. Yet time trend data for TFA in groundwater remain scarce, despite growing concern about TFA as a persistent groundwater contaminant. We analyzed temporal trends in official Austrian monitoring data from 2018–2019 and 2024, comprising 98 baseline sites and 107 sites in 2024, including 16 sites sampled in both periods. TFA increased at all paired sites; mean concentrations rose from 1.36 to 2.86 µg/L (+110%) and median concentrations from 1.01 to 2.05 µg/L (+103%). Across the complete, largely non-paired datasets, mean concentrations were 0.78 and 2.42 µg/L and median concentrations were 0.39 and 1.40 µg/L, respectively. This comparison supports the hypothesis of a broader upward shift in TFA groundwater concentration on a national scale. To assess agriculture as a possible source, we tested associations with agricultural contamination indicators. TFA was associated with nitrate and pesticide burden, but not with other monitored PFAS. This supports an agricultural contribution in the most impacted regions. Given TFA's persistence and limited removal by conventional water treatment, limiting further emissions from TFA-forming pesticides and other sources, such as fluorinated gases, is important to prevent further accumulation.
items.authors: Helmut Burtscher-Schaden, Thilo Hofmann, Angeliki Lyssimachou, Mattias Öberg, Hans Peter H. Arp

items.title: Reading the whole corpus: a reproducible cross-sample Raman workflow for materials characterisation, with a spectral 3D Gaussian splatting representation for hyperspectral maps
items.abstract: Raman mapping produces a hyperspectral cube, and turning that cube into numbers depends strongly on a chain of preprocessing choices. Two further problems appear once a laboratory holds many maps rather than one: the corpus is analysed one file at a time, and the analysable corpus is only the subset somebody remembered to export by hand from the instrument’s proprietary format. We present RAMANSP, a compact open framework providing typed spectral containers, composable preprocessing protocols and an analysis layer, and extend it in three directions. First, a direct reader for the undocumented Horiba LabSpec 6 container, reverse engineered here and verified bit identical against the instrument’s own text export, which removes the manual export step and takes this corpus from 1 usable map to 23. Second, a cross-sample knowledge graph linking every acquisition by spectral similarity, shared unmixing endmembers and disorder-metric proximity, with each metric edge carrying the preprocessing protocol under which it was computed. Third, and as the main methodological contribution, spectral 3D Gaussian splatting: a map V (x,y,ν) is represented by a differentiable field of anisotropic ellipsoids, each localising a domain in the two spatial axes and a band along the wavenumber axis, fitted by first-order descent on closed-form gradients, entirely in NumPy on a CPU. On an anonymised corpus of 108 acquisitions the graph recovers 23 communities at modularity Q = 0.65 and flags 5 groups of byte-identical duplicates, and across 6 maps the field reconstructs held-out wavenumber channels to within 0.70 to 1.34 of each map’s own measurement noise at 8.1 to 37.7× compression, that is, essentially to the noise floor.
items.authors: Siddhartha Pahari, Jainish Shailesh Solanki

items.title: Redox-Promoted Reactivity of Uranium, Neptunium, and Plutonium Diamide Complexes
items.abstract: The chemically active 5 f orbitals of the early actinides give rise to a number of accessible oxidation states, as well as contribute to complex redox behavior that is sensitive to changes in the coordination environment of the metal. Understanding how these electronic and coordination effects translate into structural transformation remains a central challenge in fundamental actinide chemistry. Herein, we present a crystallographic and spectroscopic investigation of redox-promoted reactivity in uranium, neptunium, and plutonium complexes supported by malonamide and diglycolamide ligands, which provide flexible O-donor coordination environments for investigating structural chemistry of early actinides as a function of the oxidation state. A series of molecular [An VI O 2 (ma)(NO 3 ) 2 ], [An VI O 2 (tmma)(NO 3 ) 2 ], and [An VI O 2 (tmdga) 2 ](NO 3 ) 2 complexes across the U−Np−Pu series has been prepared and structurally characterized, providing a platform for examining chemical transformations induced by ligand degradation and electron transfer (ma = malonamide; tmma = N,N,N′,N′ -tetramethylmalonamide; tmdga = N,N,N′,N′- tetramethyldiglycolamide). Aging these complexes in acidic media leads to the formation of unexpected products spanning multiple oxidation states, including oxalate-bridged actinyl dimers generated through oxidative degradation of diglycolamide ligands, mixed-valent Pu(IV)/Pu(VI) molecular ion pairs, and neptunium species that evolve from monomeric Np(VI) complexes to mixed-valent Np(V)/Np(IV) assemblies featuring Np V =O yl −Np IV actinyl–actinide interactions before complete reduction to Np(IV) products. Complementary single-crystal Raman spectroscopy provides vibrational fingerprints of the actinyl units and coordinated ligands, supporting the structural assignments and enabling comparisons across the U–Np–Pu series. These results demonstrate that diamide ligands may serve as both coordination platforms and active participants in redox chemistry, giving rise to reaction pathways that generate previously inaccessible molecular species.
items.authors: Dmytro V. Kravchuk

items.title: The Design and Application of Diureido Functionalized Spiroligomers as Diphosphate Receptors
items.abstract: Spiroligomers are rigid, stereochemically defined scaffolds that can be programmed to display functional groups in precise three-dimensional constellations. We utilize this scaffold to position two urea groups in a preorganized geometry for anion binding. Among the receptors synthesized, the spiroligomer with RRRR-configuration displayed the strongest affinity for hydrogen pyrophosphate H2PPi (H2P2O7
items.authors: Yanfeng Fan, Kyle Brunner, Chongsong Xu, Owen O’Sullivan, Melody Pham, Michael J. Zdilla

items.title: Dynamic Parameter Screening for Accelerated Mechanistic Analysis
items.abstract: Mechanistic studies are essential for the continued advancement of the chemical sciences however; classical approaches remain laborious and material intensive. Graphical reaction analysis techniques such as RPKA and VTNA have substantially reduced this burden, yet the time and resources required to comprehensively study increasingly complex reactions remain high. Medium- and high-throughput batch and flow kinetic methods have been developed to further streamline data acquisition, but their widespread adoption is limited by the need for specialized equipment or expertise. Here we introduce dynamic parameter screening (DPS), in which a single batch reaction is monitored continuously while sequential reagent and catalyst additions are used to probe kinetic impacts of multiple species within one experimental setup. Using the palladium-catalyzed Kumada–Tamao–Corriu cross-coupling as a model system, we compared DPS with traditional one-factor-at-a-time approach across three catalytic systems (PdCl2(dppf)·CH2Cl2, PEPPSI-iPr, and XPhos Pd G2). DPS afforded essentially identical qualitative and quantitative (kinetic modeling) conclusions except for the case of XPhos Pd G2. This latter system exhibited multiple kinetic regimes where the traditional approach revealed the global impact of reagent concentrations, whereas DPS provided complementary, higher-resolution insight into reagent effects within a specific kinetic regime. The insights obtained from DPS guided a simple slow-dosing strategy that markedly improved reaction rates even at reduced catalyst loadings. DPS therefore provides a practical, low-barrier route to high-resolution kinetic information that is fully compatible with conventional modeling, broadening access to mechanistic understanding in resource-limited settings.
items.authors: Dylan J. Pyle, Finn Bork, Wesley McNutt, Ekaterina Trushina, Joshua S. Derasp, Sara M. Guzman

items.title: Force-Programmed Evolution of Topological Freedom in Slide-Ring Polymer Networks
items.abstract: Force-adaptive polymer networks, whose mechanical response evolves under load, offer a route to structural materials that combine high stiffness and strength with efficient energy dissipation.[1,2] Most existing force-adaptive systems achieve this through mechanochemical reactions that generate reactive intermediates and thereby stiffen or rearrange the network,[3-5] a strategy that is intrinsically limited by diffusion, reaction kinetics, and the irreversible consumption of the reactive species. Here we pursue a fundamentally different strategy, in which a force-triggered transformation regulates the topological freedom of a slide-ring crosslink[6,7] rather than driving a chemical reaction. We integrate a mechanophore directly into the stopper of a rotaxane crosslinker, in which a cyclobutane formed by the [2+2] photodimerization of two cinnamate units[8,9] acts as the bulky stopper that confines a 24-crown-8 macrocycle on a dibenzylammonium axle.[10,11] Under load, retro-[2+2] cycloreversion reduces the steric dimension of the stopper and thereby expands the sliding space accessible to the macrocycle, so that a single covalent event gates a large slidingdissipation channel rather than dissipating energy directly. We incorporated this crosslinker into a segmented polyurethane and evaluated it against an orthogonal three-member sample set (R, C1, C2) of identical crosslinker content that decouples whether the stopper can open from whether the macrocycle can slide. The optimal composition, R3, reaches a toughness of about 215 MJ m-3 and a tensile strength of about 38 MPa—up to 9.4 and 5.6 times the toughness and strength of the openbut-cannot-slide control (C1), and far exceeding the constitutively sliding control (C2). Smallstrain dynamic mechanical analysis confirms that the mechanophore is silent at low strain, whereas gradient cyclic loading reveals a force-activation fingerprint: the dissipation ratio of R3 rises from below both controls at 100% strain to above them at high strain, crossing over near 300–400%. Infrared spectroscopy detects the regenerated cinnamate C=C band only after stretching and only in the cyclobutane-bearing samples,[8,9] and an annealing-reload test shows that the extra dissipation of R3 is largely recoverable with the smallest permanent damage of the three, consistent with a reversible sliding channel that shields the matrix.[12,13] These results establish a general design principle in which the structural precision of a mechanochemical transformation programs the evolution of topological freedom during deformation.
items.authors: Chenjuan Yu, Yuping Wang

items.title: Kinetic Mechanism Development and Pollutant Chemistry in NH3/H2/CH4 Combustion
items.abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising carbon-free fuel, but because it is difficult to combust, blending ammonia with co-fuels such as H 2 and CH 4 is one approach to improve combustibility. However, the underlying chemical interactions, particularly coupled carbon–nitrogen (C–N) pathways, become increasingly complex as fuel composition expands. Existing kinetic mechanisms are typically constructed by manually merging NH 3 and hydrocarbon sub-mechanisms, often with limited systematic treatment of C–N cross chemistry and frequently involving empirical tuning of kinetic parameters. In this work, a comprehensive kinetic mechanism for NH 3 /H 2 /CH 4 combustion is developed using the Reaction Mechanism Generator without any empirical parameter tuning. The mechanism builds upon a previously validated NH 3 /H 2 model and a recent, high-quality hydrocarbon mechanism. C-N chemistry is obtained from the literature when available and automatically constructed with Reaction Mechanism Generator when not. For select important reactions, we calculated kinetic parameters in this work. The developed mechanism is validated against laminar-burning velocities, ignition-delay times, and flow-reactor and jet-stirred-reactor measurements, showing good agreement over a wide range of conditions. Using the validated model, pollutant formation and consumption pathways for NOx , N 2 O, HCN, and CO are systematically investigated across the ternary composition space.
items.authors: Sunkyu Shin, Yu-Chi Kao, Timo T. Pekkanen, Yujie Qian, Yi-Pei Li, William H. Green

items.title: Achieving Sustained Conformational Exploration with Continually Adaptive Local Memory Sampling
items.abstract: Enhanced sampling techniques aim to expedite the exploration of molecular conformations and their associated transitions. The extended adaptive biasing force method (eABF) is an enhanced sampling technique that applies a biasing force to targeted collective variables (CV), which serves to overcome energy barriers that would normally delay conformational transitions. With eABF, the biasing force is adaptively constructed to nullify the average force acting along the CV, effectively removing barriers to promote accelerated transitions. However, the eABF biasing force can become unresponsive to CV-coupled environmental dynamics, leading to hindered CV sampling. Therefore, in order to promote persistent CV transitions, we developed the continually adaptive local memory (CALM) sampling method, designed to sustain adaptation of the eABF biasing force. This is achieved by maintaining a limited sampling memory, which allows for CV moves to continually synchronize with coupled environmental dynamics. Herein, we show CALM effectively accelerates conformational sampling of alanine dipeptide and deca-alanine in vacuum and also deca-alanine and the mini-protein chignolin in explicit water. As a result of maintaining biasing force adaptability, we illustrate how CALM promotes sustained CV transitions via access to hidden conformational pathways that are not accessible via eABF.
items.authors: Steven L. Austin, H. Lee Woodcock

items.title: Investigating the ‘Water Paradox’: Theoretical Evidence for Electric Field-Mediated Catalysis of Peptide Bond Formation
items.abstract: A key question in origins of life chemistry – sometimes termed the ‘Water Paradox’ – is how complex biomolecules can form via condensation reactions in aqueous environments. This problem is exemplified by the formation of peptides, which is a challenging reaction in bulk water because high free energy barriers and small thermodynamic driving forces hinder polymerization. Recent experiments suggest that peptide polymerization is more facile at air-water interfaces, possibly due to the presence of intrinsic interfacial electric fields. Here we explore the viability of electric field catalysis of peptide bond formation using quantum mechanical simulations of the dimerization of glycine zwitterions. Our results suggest that oriented electric fields reduce the high barrier, six-step mechanism in bulk water to a simpler four-step process with substantially lower reaction barriers. Furthermore, our modeling indicates that the reverse reaction – peptide hydrolysis – is not catalyzed because the oriented electric field causes a spatial separation between the reacting water and the peptide bond, making the initial hydrolysis step less accessible. These results complement experimental findings and provide a compelling mechanism that supports the hypothesis that interfacial electric fields could play a central role in prebiotic peptide synthesis.
items.authors: Teddy Herriman, Gino A. DiLabio
items.title_zh: 探讨“水悖论”：电场介导的肽键形成催化理论证据
items.summary_zh: 生命起源化学中的一个关键问题——“水悖论”——是复杂生物分子如何在水环境中通过缩合反应形成。肽的形成是一个在水中具有挑战性的反应，因为高自由能障碍和小热力学驱动力阻碍了聚合。近期实验表明，肽聚合在气-水界面上更为容易，可能与内在的界面电场有关。本文通过量子力学模拟甘氨酸双离子的二聚化，探讨电场催化肽键形成的可行性。结果表明，定向电场将水中高能障碍的六步机制简化为反应障碍显著降低的四步过程。此外，模型显示反应的逆过程——肽水解并未被催化，因为定向电场导致反应水和肽键之间的空间分离，使初始水解步骤变得不易接近。这些结果补充了实验发现，并提供了支持界面电场在前生物肽合成中发挥核心作用的有力机制。

items.title: Tree-Based Classification of Functional Groups from IR Spectra: Feature Importance Corroborates Quantum-Chemical Fragment Frequencies
items.abstract: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy is a widely used analytical technique for identifying functional groups in chemical compounds, but its interpretation remains labor-intensive and reliant on expert knowledge, especially for complex or multicomponent samples. This study presents a tree-based Random Forest (RF) machine-learning framework, successfully developed to predict the presence of specific functional groups (FGs) from an infrared spectra database. Stratification was employed to address positive class imbalance, maintaining the F1-score drop under 12% across models. All models achieved strong overall performance, with accuracy, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and out-of-bag (OOB) scores exceeding 0.8. Of the 46 FGs modeled, 43 demonstrated acceptable performance, while only three underperformed, as categorized by their Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) scores. Threshold tuning further improved model performance, yielding up to a 9% increase in MCC score. Finally, feature importance extracted from the trained models exhibited strong interpretability, correlating with theoretically predicted IR spectra and bridging experimental data with theoretical chemical significance. These results establish a robust, interpretable framework with potential for integration into intelligent monitoring and process optimization systems.
items.authors: Muhammad Khari Secario, Shingjiang Jessie Lue

items.title: Leveraging Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials into Fitting Fast and Accurate AMBER-Compatible Precise Force Field
items.abstract: Transferable force fields enable routine molecular dynamics simulations across broad chemical space, but finite transferable parameter sets may not describe unusual chemical environments with uniform accuracy.Here, we present ParmFit, an automated preciseforce-field parameterization framework within MAPLE that uses machine-learning interatomic potentials to efficiently construct and refine AMBER/GAFF-compatible parameters.ParmFit extends this strategy across small molecules, chemically modified biomolecular residues, and metal coordination environments while selectively retaining compatible force field terms.In a challenging subset of FreeSolv, UMA-based precise parameters reduced the average hydration free-energy prediction error by more than 1 kcal mol -1 , while ParmFit-generated models of covalently modified proteins and metalloproteins maintained stable structural and coordination behavior in molecular dynamics simulations.By integrating efficient MLIP calculations, selective parameter refinement, and direct compatibility with established force-field workflows, ParmFit provides a practical route toward broader use of precise force fields in molecular simulation.
